Dockistrate End-to-End Flow and Function Reference

This document explains how Dockistrate runs in both interactive and CLI modes and documents every Bash function in the repo. It is intentionally verbose and focuses on what happens under the hood: inputs, validation, file/state changes, Docker actions, and call paths. Completion scripts and test harness/test case functions are included later in a compact format to keep the reference exhaustive.

Key conventions used in this file:

  • "Entry points" explains how a function is reached. Unless noted, CLI and interactive both call the same function via run_command.
  • "Reads/Writes" lists the main state/config files or Docker resources the function touches.
  • "Side effects" calls out container changes, file mutations, and backups.
  • "Interactive notes" only appear when the function behaves differently under INTERACTIVE=true.
  • Messages prefixed with [Error] are emitted to stderr so stdout remains parseable for automation.

Operator walkthroughs

Use the documentation index for illustrated, task-based interactive

walkthroughs. The command index links every menu

command to its procedure. Screenshots and short explanations live in those

guides; this reference retains implementation, state, and call-path detail.

End-to-End Flow (Interactive vs CLI)

Entry Script: dockistrate.sh

  • Loads version, lib/config.sh, and then sources modules via lib/loader.sh.
  • Eager-loads core modules needed for dispatch (logging, utils, dependencies, cli) and source-only domain configuration discovery.
  • Initializes global flags: VERBOSE=false, INTERACTIVE=false.
  • Performs a lightweight pre-scan of argv to allow version, fix-permissions, restore-backup, domain configuration commands, and pre-runtime update helpers (help, help update, help-update, upgrade-preflight) to avoid normal runtime prep before dispatch. Domain validation and preview must work with unfinished drafts; apply and migration own their activation path.
  • Parses -v/--verbose and -i/--interactive flags.
  • If verbose and a runtime command has been selected: prepares log capture via ensure_log_writable and enables tracing through xtrace_start. Each trace block begins with one wall-clock anchor; each [CMD] prefix uses a session ID and elapsed whole seconds without launching a clock process. Trace gating honors redacted visibility and sensitive arguments; a failed settings load keeps tracing disabled before runtime preparation.
  • Defers full runtime prep until the first real command path; prep sources deferred feature modules, then runs check_dependencies, load_config, and cleanup_leftovers once per process. fix-permissions and pre-runtime update helpers skip this path; restore-backup waits until its candidate passes intake and configuration validation.
  • If interactive: enters the task-oriented picker loop via interactive_picker, prepares runtime when a runtime command is selected, collects args via prompt_args_for_command, reviews mutating commands via review_command_before_run, dispatches via run_command, and records successful runtime-command selections through interactive_record_recent_command. Permission repair skips runtime preparation, audit logging, and saved-command writes. Restore defers preparation and audit logging until candidate validation and records history only after a completed restore.
  • If CLI: prepares runtime immediately before dispatch unless the command is pre-runtime, then calls run_command.

Interactive Mode Flow

  1. dockistrate.sh sets INTERACTIVE=true.
  2. interactive_picker shows the home screen, task submenus, global search, or the advanced command browser.
  3. When a command is chosen, deferred runtime prep runs once (module load + dependency checks + config load) unless the command is permission repair, backup restore, a domain configuration command, or a pre-runtime update helper. Restore performs its own prep after confirming and validating the candidate. Domain configuration prompts can select invalid drafts; validation and preview do not prepare live state.
  4. prompt_args_for_command (or specialized collectors) gathers args, validates input, and sends mutating commands through review_command_before_run.
  5. When the review is accepted, SELECTED_CMD/SELECTED_ARGS are set; choosing Edit re-enters argument collection for the same command, and Cancel returns to the picker.
  6. run_command is called with the selected command and arguments.
  7. Successful interactive runtime-command selections, including operator-entered Docker option, header, and generic Nginx directive values in default full mode, are stored privately in state/config/interactive_recent.csv; redacted mode skips affected selections. Completed restores are recorded, while canceled restores are omitted. Recents and favorites rerun through the same review path and honor the preparation/logging exceptions for repair and restore commands.
  8. The same core functions are executed as in CLI mode. Some functions check INTERACTIVE for prompts or defaults.

CLI Mode Flow

  1. dockistrate.sh parses flags and sets INTERACTIVE=false.
  2. Deferred runtime prep runs once (module load + dependency checks + config load), except for permission repair and pre-runtime update helpers. Backup restore defers this prep until candidate validation.
  3. run_command dispatches based on the command name.
  4. Commands validate input and run the same core functions as interactive mode.

Execution Flags and Behaviors

  • INTERACTIVE: enables prompts and menu selection logic. Some functions treat empty values as "keep current" in interactive mode.
  • VERBOSE: enables shell tracing, logs command traces, and prints verbose messages. Trace prefixes use [session=<pid> elapsed=<seconds>s] [CMD] with one wall-clock session anchor; full trace detail and visibility gates are unchanged. Elapsed time is relative to the current trace block: each interactive runtime-command selection starts a new anchor, then log capture stops before the picker resumes. Permission repair and pre-runtime update helpers skip verbose log-file setup, including saved-command replay. Restore starts log capture only after candidate validation and retains the redacted-visibility trace gate.

The diagnostic trace prefix differs from 1.0.1's per-line calendar timestamp.

Trace parsers must use the session anchor and elapsed field; ordinary audit and

application-log timestamps are unchanged. This applies to CLI and interactive

tracing with no new command/flag flow or state migration. See

verbose trace timing.

Internal test/orchestration controls exist in the codebase (for example, skip-Docker or skip-update switches), but they are not part of the supported operator configuration surface.

State and Configuration Layout

Environment variables:

Dockistrate does not expose operator-facing environment-variable overrides for

runtime roots or proxy identity. Internal test/orchestration controls mentioned

elsewhere in this file are not part of the supported operator configuration

surface.

Main state directory: state/.

Runtime state paths are guarded before creation, writes, and permission

normalization. Symlinked state roots or subdirectories such as state/config,

state/logs, state/certs, state/acme-webroot, and generated Nginx config

directories fail closed instead of being followed.

Domain configuration schema 5 groups each domain under

state/domains/<normalized-domain>/. Its config/ contains editable,

purpose-specific CSV files; runtime/applied/ contains the last successful

snapshot; runtime/ contains managed identities and operational metadata;

generated/, certs/, and mtls/ contain domain-owned output and material.

Aliases, dedicated hosts, and certificate-only owners each have their own

directory. Shared defaults and listener-wide settings remain global.

Manual edits require apply-domain-config <domain>|--all. Existing CLI and

interactive mutations remain immediate when their target has no pending edits.

The pending check follows each command's target: host-specific changes use the

named host, port/path and backend runtime changes resolve the primary backend,

and backend removal also checks dependent hosts. Global values are not inferred

to be domain selectors.

Normal rendering and lookup use applied state, so an invalid draft does not

disable unrelated commands. Missing domain folders never imply deletion.

See Domain configuration files for the exact

CSV headers, examples, explicit-clearing semantics, and migration workflow.

Security-rule files use rule_id,order,enabled,action,mode,status_code,reason,source_location; conditions remain in their separate table. Explicit migration maps all older rules to Require while retaining IDs, global order, inheritance and separate editable/applied snapshots. It changes storage without activating drafts or changing services.

Key files (paths are resolved in lib/config/common.sh):

  • Fixed proxy container identity: nginx-proxy (commands refuse to manage a conflicting third-party container or another Dockistrate checkout’s proxy with that name).
  • state/config/state_schema_version: runtime state schema marker. Legacy shared state is schema 1; vertical per-domain settings are schema 2; named-field records with split listener/certificate options are schema 3; consolidated listener/certificate records are schema 4; explicit security-rule actions are schema 5. migrate-state performs the versioned conversion; newer unsupported versions fail validation.
  • state/config/global_settings.csv: header enable_auto_backups,backup_retention,enable_backup_compression,http_version,client_ip_header,proxy_ip_header,tls_protocols,tls_ciphers,security_rule_status,acl_status,acl_policy,trusted_proxy_ranges,real_ip_recursive,nginx_directive_strict,nginx_docker_opts,visibility_policy,nginx_image,certbot_image,nginx_pull_mode,certbot_pull_mode, followed by one values record. Reordered columns are accepted; ignored extension columns are retained.
  • state/config/backend_ports.csv: mixed record types with header record_type,domain,backend_upstream,network,path_prefix,header_set,listen_port,upstream_port,protocol,certificate_ref,websocket,redirect_enabled,redirect_code,http3_enabled,alt_svc,path_match,path_priority,path_target,path_rewrite,reason,source_location.
    • Backend rows (record_type=backend) use domain,backend_upstream,network.
    • Port rows (record_type=port) use domain,listen_port,upstream_port,protocol,certificate_ref,websocket,redirect_enabled,redirect_code,http3_enabled,alt_svc.
    • Path rows (record_type=path) use domain,path_prefix,header_set,listen_port,websocket,redirect_enabled,redirect_code,path_match,path_priority,path_target,path_rewrite,reason,source_location.
  • state/config/backend_identity.csv: private header domain,container_id,ownership_token; one normalized domain, full immutable container ID and launch token per managed backend. New launches write it transactionally. Existing identity-less deployments use explicit update-backend --replace-unmanaged-container <full-id> --image <image> replacement; no name-based adoption.
  • state/config/nginx_directives.csv: header scope,domain,listen_port,path_prefix,directive_mode,directive_name,directive_value (scope: global|backend|port|path|stream-global|stream-backend|stream-port, directive_mode: managed|raw).
  • state/config/backend_aliases.csv: header record_type,hostname,target_domain (record_type is alias or dedicated).
  • state/config/dedicated_host_inheritance.csv: header hostname,inherit_mtls,inherit_acl,inherit_security_rules,inherit_headers,inherit_paths.
  • state/config/custom_headers.csv: header header_type,header_name,header_value.
  • state/config/backend_headers.csv: header domain,header_type,header_name,header_value.
  • state/config/backend_http_versions.csv: header domain,http_version.
  • state/config/port_tls_protocols.csv: header listen_port,tls_protocols.
  • state/config/port_tls_ciphers.csv: header listen_port,tls_ciphers.
  • state/config/capture_tls_decrypt.state: TLS key capture session state (enabled, keylog_file, timestamp).
  • state/config/backend_mtls.csv: header domain,mtls_directory.
  • state/config/backend_client_ip_headers.csv: header domain,client_ip_header_name.
  • state/config/backend_proxy_ip_headers.csv: header domain,proxy_ip_header_name.
  • state/config/backend_docker_opts.csv: header domain,docker_options; normalized domain identities have no backend: prefix.
  • state/config/backend_acl_policies.csv: header domain,acl_policy.
  • state/config/backend_acl_statuses.csv: header domain,acl_status_code.
  • state/config/backend_security_rule_statuses.csv: header domain,security_rule_status_code.
  • state/config/security_rules.csv: CSV rule DB with header enabled,domain,mode,status_code,condition_count,selector_1,name_1,condition_1,value_1,selector_2,name_2,condition_2,value_2,selector_3,name_3,condition_3,value_3,selector_4,name_4,condition_4,value_4,selector_5,name_5,condition_5,value_5,selector_6,name_6,condition_6,value_6,selector_7,name_7,condition_7,value_7,selector_8,name_8,condition_8,value_8,selector_9,name_9,condition_9,value_9,selector_10,name_10,condition_10,value_10,reason,source_location,action.
  • state/config/security_ip_rules.csv: CSV rule DB with header enabled,domain,scope,action,ip_value,status_code.
  • state/config/access_log_fields.csv: header log_field (one Nginx log variable per row for log_format).
  • state/config/interactive_recent.csv: interactive-only recent successful command selections, header timestamp,command,arg_count,args_csv, capped at 10 entries.
  • state/config/interactive_favorites.csv: interactive-only saved command selections, header command,arg_count,args_csv.

After migration, the per-domain aggregate files above are generated

compatibility views for existing command implementations. Edit the domain's

config/ files, not backend_ports.csv or the generated aggregate override

tables. Global settings and saved command history retain their own ownership.

Generated Nginx config:

  • state/config/nginx_conf/nginx.conf
  • state/config/nginx_conf/conf.d/*.conf
  • state/config/nginx_conf/conf.d/security_ip/*.inc
  • state/config/nginx_conf/stream_conf/*.conf
  • state/config/nginx_conf/stream_conf/security_ip/*.inc

Runtime directories:

  • state/domains/<domain>/certs/<certificate_id>/ for owned certificate material, and state/domains/<domain>/mtls/ for private mTLS material.
  • state/shared/acme/ and state/shared/certificate_receipts/ for shared issuer state and successful issuance receipts.
  • state/certs/ for retained legacy certificate material during migration.
  • state/logs/ for logs.
  • state/backups/ for backups and transaction archives.
  • state/pcaps/ for packet captures.
  • state/tmp/ for temp files.

Default runtime permission policy:

  • Directories: state, config, logs, logs/errors, acme-webroot, certs -> 750.
  • Directories: tmp, pcaps, backups -> 700.
  • Files: new global_settings.csv -> 640; existing global settings retain tighter modes under a 640 ceiling, and ordinary saves preserve their numeric owner/group.
  • Files: state_schema_version -> 640.
  • Files: interactive_recent.csv, interactive_favorites.csv, docker_manager.log, audit.log, audit.log.1 -> 600.
  • Files: backend_docker_opts.csv, capture_tls_decrypt.state, *.tar.gz, *.pcap -> 600.

Saved-command and Dockistrate log files require private access before their

contents are read/written; runtime preparation and fix-permissions tighten

existing copies. Failed private-access checks prevent persistence; logging

failure does not echo the raw message as a fallback. This changes group-reader

access from 1.0.1, without changing CSV formats, full visibility, or replay.

Global settings can hold Nginx Docker options; startup, saves, and restore enforce

their 640 ceiling without widening tighter modes. Replacements are staged

privately and verified before publication. See the

saved-settings upgrade note,

storage and retention

and the access upgrade note.

Function Reference by Module

Module: domain configuration (lib/domain_config/*.sh)

init_domain_config (lib/domain_config/commands.sh)

  • Entry points: init-domain-config <domain> [--kind backend|alias|dedicated|certificate-only], CLI and interactive.
  • Behavior: normalizes the domain and creates the complete CSV template set without overwriting an existing source directory. Backend templates require an operator-selected image and application port; alias/dedicated templates require their target.
  • Reads/Writes: state/domains/<domain>/config/.
  • Side effects: source-file creation only; no backend launch or proxy activation.

validate_domain_config (lib/domain_config/commands.sh)

  • Entry points: validate-domain-config <domain>|--all, CLI and interactive.
  • Behavior: snapshots the selected source files, combines them with unselected domains' applied snapshots, validates schemas and cross-domain references, and reports errors without activating anything. --all selects the complete desired setup.
  • Alias scope: local headers, security rules, ACLs, and ACL/security status settings are supported. Alias-local HTTP/IP settings, paths, Nginx directives, and mTLS are rejected with guidance to configure the target backend or use a dedicated host.
  • Redirect defaults: an enabled HTTP listener accepts a blank code for 301; an enabled path accepts a blank code to inherit the listener's full code and target port, then falls back to 301. Explicit invalid codes and codes paired with off or inherit remain rejected.
  • Side effects: private temporary validation files, removed after the command; no live-state initialization.

apply_domain_config (lib/domain_config/apply.sh)

  • Entry points: apply-domain-config <domain>|--all [--dry-run], CLI and interactive.
  • Behavior: preview validates and reports the proposed operation; apply reconciles declared backends and certificates, builds configuration, and publishes the selected applied snapshots transactionally. The declared backend state includes running or stopped. Existing ownership checks and runtime recovery protect managed resources.
  • Redirect defaults work in both CLI and interactive mode, including dedicated-host inherited paths. Saved blank codes stay blank, so later listener changes continue to update inherited path redirects instead of freezing an earlier default.
  • Network and lifecycle: a network change on a stopped backend updates its actual attachment without requiring an assigned IP. If the same draft changes state to running, apply moves the attachment while stopped, starts the container, and records its current IP. A failed network change rolls back without publishing the draft in either CLI or interactive mode.
  • Reads/Writes: selected domain source files; domain runtime/generated/certificate material; generated shared configuration and compatibility views.
  • Activation: security-policy changes use the same proxy recreation/readiness boundary as CLI/menu mutations; preview reports recreation. Successful changed applies request one finalized automatic backup when enabled, including file-only edits. Unchanged applies do neither.
  • Candidate validation: the temporary Nginx container retains runtime capabilities and environment but omits serving endpoint identities such as static IP/MAC addresses and network aliases. It forces foreground, noninteractive execution after operator flags, including shorthand bundles, so the actual Nginx validation exit status gates activation. Saved serving options remain unchanged.
  • Failure behavior: restores the previous applied/runtime state and preserves edited source files, including concurrent edits. Missing source never implies domain destruction.
  • Generated layout: the first apply after migration refreshes domain artifacts and the proxy layout even when source and applied declarations match. Preview reports that refresh. A renderer version marker is written only after successful rendering and rolls back with generated configuration; diagnostic placeholders cannot make an unrendered layout current.
  • Interactive notes: Review is the default action and needs no mutation confirmation. Apply uses the ordinary command review.

Domain mTLS preparation (lib/domain_config/certificates_mtls.sh)

  • _domain_config_mtls_state_mode <output-var> <domain> <dir> distinguishes permitted first-time creation from existing authority reuse. A previously enabled authority remains existing even when its directory is missing; restore always requires existing material.
  • domain_config_preflight_mtls <candidate> validates selected enabled authorities and inherited dedicated-host dependencies before material or backend runtime changes. It does not initialize missing authority/history files.
  • domain_config_provision_mtls <candidate> preflights selected authorities, creates only explicitly fresh authorities, prepares derived configuration/output directories, and recovers missing CRLs from validated state.
  • _domain_restore_prepare_mtls <prepared> performs that preparation against the private restore tree. Disabled retained material and unfinished drafts remain untouched.

migrate_state (lib/domain_config/migration.sh)

  • Entry points: migrate-state [--dry-run] [--backend-details <csv>], CLI and interactive.
  • Behavior: converts complete legacy domain state into versioned domain folders. Optional backend details use domain,image,state; unresolved image/state information must be supplied instead of guessed. Preview does not migrate or bootstrap live state.
  • Missing ownership: a complete details row permits storage-only migration when a legacy backend has no saved identity, even if its container name is occupied. This does not adopt a container or create runtime identity. Existing saved identities must still verify; supplied details cannot override verified image/state. Explicit update-backend --replace-unmanaged-container <full-id> --image <image> establishes ownership afterwards in either CLI or interactive mode.
  • Compatibility: migration preserves existing routes and policy semantics; legacy numeric rule commands continue to address the corresponding migrated rules. The schema marker changes only when activation succeeds.
  • Preflight rejects duplicate backend or hostname ownership and collisions between them before export; shared HTTP listeners and certificates owned by an existing backend remain valid.
  • Running proxy: migration does not reload or replace it. The first explicit apply produces the domain-generated layout and activates it through the normal validated render path.

Domain configuration discovery and status (lib/domain_config/common.sh, lib/domain_config/candidate.sh)

  • domain_config_list [all|applied|draft] enumerates normalized domain folders without preparing the runtime. Completion uses this source-only interface.
  • domain_config_status [domain] reports applied, draft, pending changes, invalid draft, missing source, or runtime drift; the full report includes editable paths. Runtime drift means the observed managed backend differs from its applied configuration.
  • New or pending drafts receive source-only graph validation against other domains' applied snapshots, catching missing references and global listener/rule conflicts. Unrelated drafts are excluded. Unchanged applied domains retain the fast path; status does not compile, render, or activate configuration.
  • Candidate assembly uses applied snapshots for unselected domains and checks for source edits during input capture. Canonical comparison ignores quote style and line endings; explicit order fields retain rule and option ordering.

Domain CSV model (lib/domain_config/model.sh, lib/domain_config/serialization.sh)

  • Centralizes filenames, exact headers, parsing, serialization, lookups, and canonical comparison. Data is never executed as shell syntax.
  • Numeric identities are normalized in memory by lib/domain_config/numeric_values.sh: padded decimal ports and path priorities compare by value, duplicate listener spellings are rejected, and reading never rewrites an unfinished draft. Certificate IDs and suffix labels retain their storage identity.
  • Routing, path options, headers, Docker arguments, Nginx directives, certificates, ACLs, security rules, and conditions use separate small tables. Optional files may be absent; header-only tables represent no rows, while a present zero-byte file is invalid. Required identity/backend values remain validated.
  • The values and defaults reference lists accepted scalar/option keys, explicit blank versus absent behavior, inheritance switches, and stable IDs versus numeric CLI selectors.
  • New CLI argument choices, command metadata, review summaries, completion, and the Domain Configuration menu use the same public apply/validate/migrate behavior.

Note: Unless explicitly stated, interactive and CLI flows converge at run_command and execute the same function bodies. Interactive differences are only called out when the function reads INTERACTIVE or adds prompts.

Module: loader (lib/loader/*.sh)

_source_modules (lib/loader/_source_modules.sh)

  • Entry points: dockistrate.sh when sourcing core modules.
  • Inputs: list of file paths.
  • Behavior: sequentially source each given file.
  • Side effects: loads functions/variables into the current shell.

Module: config (lib/config/*.sh)

load_config (lib/config/load_config.sh)

  • Entry points: dockistrate_prepare_runtime in dockistrate.sh (first command path).
  • Inputs: none; relies on CONFIG_DIR, STATE_DIR, etc.
  • Behavior: parses and semantically validates every recognized global setting, rejects duplicate keys, and publishes the loaded values only after the entire file passes. Rejection leaves previous in-memory settings unchanged. Missing supported keys retain defaults, and unknown extension keys remain ignored. Runtime bootstrap validates persisted settings before schema repairs; malformed values are not silently normalized to defaults.
  • Reads/Writes: reads GLOBAL_SETTINGS_FILE after safe ancestry, regular-file, and single-link checks; broad mode bits alone do not prevent read-only semantic validation.
  • Side effects: updates in-memory global settings only; does not change permissions. Runtime bootstrap secures validated settings before schema/migration writes.

validate_settings_for_render (lib/config/persisted_settings.sh)

  • Entry points: runtime preparation, staged backup validation, and update_nginx_config.
  • Behavior: validates loaded global settings, six backend HTTP/header/ACL override files, and dedicated-host inheritance before rendering or runtime preparation. Reads every override row, rejects malformed or duplicate normalized domains, preserves intentional header disabling and inheritance no, and reports invalid settings without echoing their values.
  • Reads/Writes: reads persisted CSV files; does not rewrite them. Runtime bootstrap retains initialization of an empty regular global settings file; restore preflight does not permit empty files.

_with_validated_render_settings (lib/config/persisted_settings.sh)

  • Entry points: update_nginx_config.
  • Behavior: validates captured override/inheritance contents once per render and retains normalized rows in local Bash 3-compatible arrays. Getters reuse those rows only within this scope and reject content or file-type changes before reuse. Standalone getters still validate every row; failed preflight never invokes rendering, and later renders start with fresh snapshots.
  • Failure handling: preflight or returned renderer failures roll back an active transaction. Exit-mode commands abort even under conditional interactive dispatch; return-mode library callers receive failure without exiting their shell. A failed preflight without an active transaction returns failure without creating one. The renderer callback remains outside a conditional so normal CLI errexit handling is retained.
  • Domain mutations: the six validated backend override schemas and dedicated-host inheritance match logical domain keys after normalization. Updates write one lowercase key, removals match mixed-case stored keys, and unrelated CSV keys and setting values retain case-sensitive behavior.

validate_persisted_config_dir (lib/config/persisted_settings.sh)

  • Entry points: runtime bootstrap and restore_backup.
  • Behavior: validates a configuration directory in an isolated shell so a rejected snapshot cannot change live in-memory settings. Restore performs this check before starting a transaction or replacing live files, then loads accepted restored globals before regeneration. Missing optional files retain existing defaults.

state_schema_bootstrap (lib/config/state_schema.sh)

  • Entry points: bootstrap_config_runtime.
  • Behavior: validates the state schema marker and initializes schema 5 for a fresh installation. Existing schema 1, 2, 3, or 4 state requires explicit migrate-state; runtime bootstrap does not convert it. Invalid or newer unsupported schema values are rejected.
  • Reads/Writes: state/config/state_schema_version.
  • Side effects: atomically creates a missing current marker only when no legacy state is detected. Existing current markers are not rewritten; explicit migration publishes its marker separately after conversion succeeds.

state_schema_version_file (lib/config/state_schema.sh)

  • Entry points: state schema bootstrap helpers and tests.
  • Behavior: returns the schema marker path under the current CONFIG_DIR.

_state_schema_normalize_version (lib/config/state_schema.sh)

  • Entry points: state schema marker read, write, and migration helpers.
  • Behavior: validates schema versions as positive bounded numeric values, strips leading zeroes, and rejects values too large for portable shell arithmetic.

_state_schema_read_marker (lib/config/state_schema.sh)

  • Entry points: state_schema_bootstrap.
  • Behavior: validates the schema marker as a single positive numeric value, preserves final lines without trailing newlines, rejects multiline marker content, and rejects newer versions than this release supports.

_state_schema_read_marker_for_supported (lib/config/state_schema.sh)

  • Entry points: upgrade_preflight and _state_schema_read_marker.
  • Behavior: read-only marker check against a supplied supported schema version. Missing marker is schema 1; malformed, multiline, overlarge, or newer unsupported markers fail without writing state.

state_schema_read_marker_readonly (lib/config/state_schema.sh)

  • Entry points: upgrade_preflight.
  • Behavior: public read-only wrapper for checking the current on-disk schema marker without creating, repairing, or migrating state.

_state_schema_write_marker (lib/config/state_schema.sh)

  • Entry points: state_schema_bootstrap.
  • Behavior: writes the schema marker atomically with restricted file mode.

_state_schema_migrate (lib/config/state_schema.sh)

  • Entry points: state_schema_bootstrap.
  • Behavior: prevents implicit startup migration. Schemas 1–4 fail with instructions to run migrate-state --dry-run, then migrate-state; the explicit domain migration command converts them to current schema 5. Unknown older schemas fail without changing the marker.

save_config (lib/config/save_config.sh)

  • Entry points: called by global settings setters.
  • Inputs: in-memory globals like HTTP_VERSION, NGINX_IMAGE, etc.
  • Behavior: writes current values in a private same-filesystem staging directory, verifies metadata, and atomically replaces GLOBAL_SETTINGS_FILE. New files use 640; existing files retain numeric owner/group and their mode intersected with 640. Unsafe paths/types/links, metadata failures, or target identity changes abort publication.
  • Side effects: replaces the global settings file only after verification; failures use the active transaction rollback path.

_finalize_global_settings_file (lib/config/settings_file.sh)

  • Entry points: _save_config_atomic_write.
  • Behavior: verifies private staging identity, retains existing numeric owner/group and tighter modes under 640, rechecks the original destination, and verifies atomic publication. Fresh files retain the destination directory's inherited group. Errors propagate to the caller; active transactions retain their existing rollback policy.

_ensure_global_settings_file_permissions_if_exists (lib/permissions/common.sh)

  • Entry points: validated bootstrap, runtime permissions, and private restore staging.
  • Behavior: rejects unsafe paths/types/links, applies the current mode intersected with 640, and verifies unchanged file identity and ownership. Missing settings are left for normal initialization; read-only load_config does not call this mutating helper.

normalize_image_with_latest (lib/config/normalize_image_with_latest.sh)

  • Entry points: load_config, set_certbot_image.
  • Inputs: image reference.
  • Behavior: appends :latest when no tag/digest is provided.
  • Returns: normalized image string.

image_uses_latest_tag (lib/config/image_uses_latest_tag.sh)

  • Entry points: pull_image_if_autopull, describe_image_with_local_state.
  • Inputs: image reference.
  • Behavior: detects if the image uses the :latest tag (not a digest).

pull_image_if_autopull (lib/config/pull_image_if_autopull.sh)

  • Entry points: recreate_nginx_container, certbot flows.
  • Inputs: image, label.
  • Behavior: validates the reference and skips explicit pulls when SKIP_DOCKER_CHECKS=true. For NGINX_IMAGE/CERTBOT_IMAGE, a digest or non-latest tag skips explicit pulls in every mode; :latest with always or if-missing attempts a pull, while never skips it. A failed pull warns and permits local fallback. Docker may still fetch a missing image during container creation; never is not an offline guarantee. Tags are mutable; only digests pin content.
  • Side effects: may docker pull the image, emits info/warn messages.

Module: runtime paths (lib/runtime_paths.sh)

The lexical helpers below preserve literal pathname bytes, including trailing

newlines. They do not resolve symlinks, inspect filesystem state, or authorize

filesystem operations; the runtime path guards perform those checks separately.

Assignment destinations must be ordinary mutable string variables, with valid

names that do not collide with the called helper's private scratch variables.

_runtime_path_strip_trailing_slashes_assign (lib/runtime_paths.sh)

  • Inputs: destination variable name, path (which may be empty).
  • Behavior: removes trailing slash characters while preserving /, then assigns the result in the caller's shell without a subprocess or stdout output.

_runtime_path_to_absolute_lexical_assign (lib/runtime_paths.sh)

  • Inputs: destination variable name, nonempty path.
  • Behavior: strips trailing slashes and prefixes relative paths with the literal PWD. It preserves internal separators and dot components; failed validation leaves the destination unchanged.

_runtime_state_declared_suffix_assign (lib/runtime_paths.sh)

  • Inputs: destination variable name, nonempty path; reads STATE_DIR.
  • Behavior: compares lexical absolute paths and assigns an empty suffix for the state root or a leading-slash suffix for a descendant. Missing inputs or paths outside that lexical prefix fail without changing the destination.

Lexical stdout wrappers (lib/runtime_paths.sh)

  • _runtime_path_strip_trailing_slashes, _runtime_path_to_absolute_lexical, and _runtime_state_declared_suffix accept a path and emit their assignment helper's result as raw bytes without an added newline.
  • Callers capturing stdout must preserve any trailing newline bytes in the pathname; internal guard callers use the assignment helpers directly.

Module: logging (lib/logging/*.sh)

log_msg (lib/logging/log_msg.sh)

  • Entry points: many command functions.
  • Inputs: message string.
  • Behavior: writes timestamped logs to owner-only LOG_FILE; honors ENABLE_LOGGING and VERBOSE. Private-access failure prevents appending and does not echo the raw message as a fallback. No built-in rotation or age limit applies.
  • Side effects: creates/updates log files, may echo to stdout/stderr.

audit_log (lib/logging/audit_log.sh)

  • Entry points: run_command (all commands).
  • Inputs: command string.
  • Behavior: normalizes control characters to single-line text and appends a timestamped attempted-command entry before dispatch, including attempts that later fail or roll back. A log larger than 1 MiB rotates on the next write to one AUDIT_LOG_FILE.1. Both files require owner-only access; private-access failure prevents persistence and raw-message fallback. There is no age-based expiry, and removing active settings does not purge audit history.
  • Side effects: writes to AUDIT_LOG_FILE.

ensure_log_writable (lib/logging/ensure_log_writable.sh)

  • Entry points: log_msg, audit_log, verbose setup.
  • Inputs: file path.
  • Behavior: rejects unsafe runtime log paths, ensures the log directory exists, fixes ownership when running as root for the invoking user, and requires owner-only 600 access before a message can be written. Reports failure if private access cannot be established; callers must not fall back to printing the raw log message.
  • Side effects: modifies permissions and ownership.

_effective_user (lib/logging/_effective_user.sh)

  • Entry points: ensure_log_writable.
  • Behavior: returns invoking user (prefers SUDO_USER when root).

ensure_root (lib/logging/ensure_root.sh)

  • Entry points: dependency installation, Docker service start.
  • Behavior: exits unless running as root.

Module: dependencies (lib/dependencies/*.sh)

check_dependencies (lib/dependencies/check_dependencies.sh)

  • Entry points: dockistrate_prepare_runtime in dockistrate.sh (first command path).
  • Behavior: runs Docker and OpenSSL checks unless SKIP_DOCKER_CHECKS=true; ensures backup dir exists.

check_docker_installed (lib/dependencies/check_docker_installed.sh)

  • Entry points: check_dependencies.
  • Behavior: verifies Docker binary; optionally installs in interactive mode.
  • Interactive notes: prompts to install Docker.

ensure_docker_running (lib/dependencies/ensure_docker_running.sh)

  • Entry points: check_dependencies.
  • Behavior: ensures Docker daemon is running; starts Docker Desktop on macOS or systemd service on Linux.
  • Interactive notes: prompts user if systemctl is unavailable.

check_docker_access (lib/dependencies/check_docker_access.sh)

  • Entry points: check_dependencies.
  • Behavior: confirms current user can run Docker commands.

check_openssl_installed (lib/dependencies/check_openssl_installed.sh)

  • Entry points: check_dependencies.
  • Behavior: verifies openssl is available; can install in interactive mode.

install_package (lib/dependencies/install_package.sh)

  • Entry points: dependency installers.
  • Behavior: installs packages via Homebrew (macOS) or apt/yum (Linux).

Module: utils (lib/utils/*.sh)

_secure_fs_pin_directory (lib/utils/secure_fs.sh)

  • Entry points: certificate snapshot, capture-output and permission-repair workers.
  • Behavior: walks absolute physical paths in a dedicated subshell, comparing each directory entry with the entered directory's device/inode before further work. Repeated separators are normalized; dot components and symlinked ancestors are rejected except for the fixed macOS /tmp and /var aliases. Mutations use the verified working directory or a verified open file handle, retaining their target if a pathname is replaced.
  • Side effects: changes the worker's current directory; the explicit create policy may create missing components privately. The allow-missing policy performs no writes.

_secure_fs_with_file (lib/utils/secure_fs.sh)

  • Entry points: regular-file reads and permission changes in the security-sensitive filesystem helpers.
  • Behavior: bounds read-only file acquisition, verifies the opened file's identity, type, link count and metadata, and runs a callback on the retained handle. A supervisor reaps the worker before the caller continues. Darwin metadata uses native stat on its stdin descriptor, avoiding /dev/fd permission masking. No writable-open or unchecked-path fallback is used; an unreadable target requires sufficient privileges.
  • Mode changes: handles Darwin chmod skipping a masked mode by using an exact, restrictive intermediate mode on regular files. This adds no read/write/execute access; the permission journal records the intermediate so an interrupted change can be rolled back.

_secure_fs_run_fresh (lib/utils/secure_fs.sh)

  • Entry points: permission metadata and certificate snapshot workers.
  • Behavior: starts the current Bash interpreter with a fixed helper source and function, passing arguments literally and preserving stdin, stdout and exit status. Clears shell startup hooks and resets HUP/INT/TERM dispositions before execution, so Bash 3 recovery does not replay an active HUP/TERM trap during worker acknowledgment. The same verified-handle checks and bounded acquisition apply inside the fresh process.

_realpath_portable (lib/utils/fs.sh)

  • Entry points: normalize_cert_dir, relativize_cert_dir.
  • Behavior: resolves absolute path without relying on GNU-only tools; preserves literal filename bytes, including trailing newlines, in native and fallback resolution. Returns a raw path without an output-line delimiter; callers must preserve trailing newlines when capturing it.

normalize_domain (lib/utils/validators.sh)

  • Entry points: most domain functions.
  • Behavior: lowercases domains for consistent matching.

sanitize_domain_name (lib/utils/validators.sh)

  • Entry points: container naming and file naming.
  • Behavior: replaces non-alphanumerics with -.

is_valid_domain (lib/utils/validators.sh)

  • Entry points: input validation.
  • Behavior: regex validation for domain format.

is_valid_port (lib/utils/validators.sh)

  • Entry points: port input validation.
  • Behavior: decimal 1..65535 validation without octal interpretation or arithmetic overflow.

Decimal numeric normalization (lib/utils/numbers.sh)

  • normalize_decimal_number validates digits, removes leading zeros, and checks a decimal ceiling before arithmetic. normalize_positive_decimal also rejects zero; normalize_port enforces 1..65535.
  • Entry points: rule/log-field IDs, path priorities, listener and upstream ports. CLI and interactive operations use the same decimal meanings; globally displayed rule IDs remain positions.

Path and redirect port normalization (lib/utils/validators.sh)

  • Normalizes the numeric port inside an upstream host:port target or status:port redirect without changing the host or status.

is_valid_optional_port (lib/utils/validators.sh)

  • Entry points: certificate port suffix prompts.
  • Behavior: allows empty or valid port.

is_valid_protocol (lib/utils/validators.sh)

  • Entry points: backend/port commands.
  • Behavior: accepts http|https|tcp|udp.

is_valid_http_version (lib/utils/validators.sh)

  • Entry points: CLI validators.
  • Behavior: accepts http1.0|http1.1|http2.

is_valid_header_name (lib/utils/validators.sh)

  • Entry points: header setters.
  • Behavior: strict header token validation.

is_header_or_off (lib/utils/validators.sh)

  • Entry points: CLI validators for header overrides.
  • Behavior: allows off or valid header name.

is_status_code (lib/utils/validators.sh)

  • Entry points: ACL/security status setters.
  • Behavior: validates HTTP status 100-599.

is_yes_no (lib/utils/validators.sh)

  • Entry points: ws and expose flags.
  • Behavior: accepts yes|no.

is_on_off (lib/utils/validators.sh)

  • Entry points: set-port-redirect, real IP recursive.
  • Behavior: accepts on|off.

is_true_false (lib/utils/validators.sh)

  • Entry points: auto backup and compression flags.
  • Behavior: accepts true|false.

is_valid_pull_mode (lib/utils/validators.sh)

  • Entry points: set-nginx-image, set-certbot-image, and interactive pull-mode prompts.
  • Behavior: accepts always|if-missing|never.

is_valid_visibility_policy (lib/utils/validators.sh)

  • Entry points: set-visibility-policy, config bootstrap.
  • Behavior: accepts full|redacted.

dockistrate_start_verbose_logging (dockistrate.sh)

  • Entry points: verbose CLI runtime dispatch and interactive runtime-command selection.
  • Behavior: prepares private log capture only when needed, selects the supported Bash trace destination, and starts a new trace block with the existing elapsed-time prefix and visibility handling.

dockistrate_stop_verbose_logging (dockistrate.sh)

  • Entry points: pre-runtime interactive selection, completion of an interactive command, and picker exit.
  • Behavior: disables tracing, restores the original stderr or closes the dedicated trace descriptor, and resets local trace-routing state so later permission repair cannot append to an active runtime log.

xtrace_start (lib/utils/runtime.sh)

  • Entry points: dockistrate.sh verbose setup after trace-destination preparation.
  • Behavior: captures one wall-clock start time with timezone offset and the initial Bash SECONDS value, installs a session/elapsed [CMD] prefix using builtin expansion, then enables tracing. A traced no-op writes the start anchor through the same destination even if ordinary application logging is disabled. Subsequent trace prefixes launch no clock subprocess; Bash 3 remains supported.
  • Side effects: sets PS4 and the trace-start counter and enables shell tracing. Existing trace suppression/restoration and command arguments are unchanged.

operator_visibility helpers (lib/utils/operator_visibility.sh)

  • Entry points: audit formatting, status/list/show output, interactive prompts, recents/favorites, and review screens.
  • Behavior: returns the active VISIBILITY_POLICY, classifies Docker option, header-value, and generic Nginx directive-value args, and returns [REDACTED] for display/history/audit copies only when the policy is redacted. Full mode remains the default and preserves displayed values. Execution inputs, stored state, and generated runtime config retain real values; switching policies does not erase existing logs or saved history.

is_valid_ipv4 (lib/utils/validators.sh)

  • Entry points: IP validation helpers.
  • Behavior: checks IPv4 format and octet ranges.

is_valid_cidr (lib/utils/validators.sh)

  • Entry points: trusted proxies, ACL.
  • Behavior: IPv4 CIDR validation.

is_valid_ip_or_cidr (lib/utils/validators.sh)

  • Entry points: ACL/trusted proxy validation.
  • Behavior: accepts IPv4 or CIDR.

is_valid_image_ref (lib/utils/validators.sh)

  • Entry points: image setters, persisted settings validation, and Docker image consumers.
  • Behavior: checks the complete Docker image reference, rejecting option-shaped names, whitespace/control characters, and malformed syntax. Supports registry ports, IPv6 registry hosts, tags, digests, repeated hyphens, and double underscores in repository components.

is_valid_network_name (lib/utils/validators.sh)

  • Entry points: nginx render-time state validation.
  • Behavior: validates Docker network names in backend state rows.

is_valid_redirect_code_spec (lib/utils/validators.sh)

  • Entry points: nginx render-time state validation.
  • Behavior: validates redirect status codes (301|302|308) with optional target port suffix (:port).

file_exists (lib/utils/fs.sh)

  • Entry points: certificate upload prompts.
  • Behavior: returns success if file exists.

normalize_cert_dir (lib/utils/certs.sh)

  • Entry points: certificate paths in add_cert, add_port, update_port, etc.
  • Behavior: normalizes certificate path under CERTS_DIR; allows external absolute paths only when explicitly enabled by callers; keeps relative traversal outside CERTS_DIR blocked.

relativize_cert_dir (lib/utils/certs.sh)

  • Entry points: certificate path storage.
  • Behavior: converts absolute certificate paths back to CERTS_DIR-relative form for storage.

is_existing_cert_dir (lib/utils/certs.sh)

  • Entry points: CLI validator.
  • Behavior: validates that a certificate directory exists under CERTS_DIR.

backend_aliases_file (lib/utils/state_helpers.sh)

  • Entry points: alias CRUD.
  • Behavior: resolves alias file path; sets BACKEND_ALIASES_FILE if not set.

backend_exists (lib/utils/state_helpers.sh)

  • Entry points: most backend operations.

alias_exists (lib/utils/state_helpers.sh)

  • Entry points: alias CRUD.
  • Behavior: checks backend_aliases.csv for an alias record.

backend_for_alias (lib/utils/state_helpers.sh)

  • Entry points: resolve alias to backend.

primary_domain_for (lib/utils/state_helpers.sh)

  • Entry points: domain resolution.
  • Behavior: resolves alias to primary backend or returns normalized input.

domain_exists (lib/utils/state_helpers.sh)

  • Entry points: header/ACL/backends.
  • Behavior: returns true if domain is backend or alias.

list_domain_aliases (lib/utils/state_helpers.sh)

  • Entry points: Nginx config, listing.
  • Behavior: lists aliases mapped to a domain.

container_exists (lib/utils/docker.sh)

  • Entry points: container ops.
  • Behavior: checks docker for container existence.

remove_container_and_anonymous_volumes (lib/utils/docker.sh)

  • Entry points: container-removal flows.
  • Behavior: removes a container via docker rm -f -v, cleaning up attached anonymous volumes.

container_status (lib/utils/docker.sh)

  • Entry points: status reports.
  • Behavior: returns Docker container state string.

container_running (lib/utils/docker.sh)

  • Entry points: start/capture/status.
  • Behavior: wraps container_status equality to running.

container_published_ports (lib/utils/docker.sh)

  • Entry points: nginx update logic.
  • Behavior: returns sorted host ports published by a container.

is_host_port_listening (lib/utils/ports_runtime.sh)

  • Entry points: listen-port preflight checks.
  • Behavior: detects whether a host TCP port is already listening (via lsof, with ss/netstat fallbacks).

port_listener_owner_info (lib/utils/ports_runtime.sh)

  • Entry points: listen-port conflict messaging.
  • Behavior: resolves pid|process ownership for a listening host port when discoverable.

is_port_mapped_in_state (lib/utils/ports_runtime.sh)

  • Entry points: listen-port preflight checks.
  • Behavior: checks whether a port is already present in Dockistrate port records, with optional skip context.

suggest_free_port (lib/utils/ports_runtime.sh)

  • Entry points: listen-port conflict messaging.

assert_host_port_available_or_fail (lib/utils/ports_runtime.sh)

  • Entry points: backend/port/nginx preflight checks.
  • Behavior: fails fast when a requested host port is occupied, prints PID/process details when available, and prints a concrete free-port recommendation when available.

ensure_network_exists (lib/utils/docker.sh)

  • Entry points: backend and nginx network operations.
  • Behavior: creates Docker network if missing.

escape_sed_literal (lib/utils/fs.sh)

  • Entry points: removal operations.

sed_in_place (lib/utils/fs.sh)

  • Entry points: most file edits.

move_line (lib/utils/fs.sh)

replace_line (lib/utils/fs.sh)

  • Entry points: security IP updates.

nginx_header_var (lib/utils/state_helpers.sh)

  • Entry points: header variable mapping.
  • Behavior: converts a header name to $http_<name> variable.

ensure_valid_or_prompt (lib/utils/prompts.sh)

  • Entry points: many command functions.
  • Behavior: validates input; in interactive mode, prompts until valid.

normalize_validated_value (lib/utils/validators.sh)

  • Entry points: ensure_valid_or_prompt.
  • Behavior: normalizes validated values (e.g., lowercasing domains).

prompt_input (lib/utils/prompts.sh)

  • Entry points: interactive flows.
  • Behavior: reads a value with a default only when INTERACTIVE=true.

prompt_input_valid (lib/utils/prompts.sh)

  • Entry points: interactive flows.
  • Behavior: repeatedly prompts until validation passes.

read_with_editing (lib/utils/fs.sh)

  • Entry points: interactive prompts.
  • Behavior: reads input with a default if empty; safe for non-tty.
  • Input status: exposes transient READ_WITH_EDITING_CANCEL_REASON=eof for aborted input while preserving its return/default contract. The backend wizard checks this status after text and multiline input and cancels without a selected command.

confirm_prompt (lib/utils/prompts.sh)

  • Entry points: destructive operations.
  • Behavior: shared confirmation helper with 2 modes. yes_no prompts when interactive and otherwise auto-confirms; strict_yes requires interactive mode and exact YES, and fails in non-interactive use.

cleanup_leftovers (lib/utils/fs.sh)

  • Entry points: dockistrate_prepare_runtime in dockistrate.sh.
  • Behavior: deletes stale nginx include files that can break config.
  • Side effects: removes specific files in NGINX_HTTP_CONF_DIR.

Module: CLI and Interactive (lib/cli/*.sh)

cli_classify_visibility_args (lib/cli/command_visibility.sh)

  • Entry points: audit/verbose command formatting, review screens, and interactive recent/favorite sensitivity checks.
  • Inputs: command name and original command arguments, with CLI or interactive argument mode.
  • Behavior: produces display-only CLI_VISIBILITY_DISPLAY_ARGS and CLI_VISIBILITY_HAS_SENSITIVE from the active visibility policy. Redacted mode recognizes actual option boundaries, fixed header-value positions, interactive backend positions, and the compact value offsets of all HTTP/stream directive scopes. Ambiguous sensitive suffixes are hidden rather than treated as new options. Full mode copies the original arguments unchanged.
  • Side effects: updates classification result variables only; does not validate, execute, or rewrite command inputs.

run_command (lib/cli/run_command.sh)

  • Entry points: dockistrate.sh (CLI or interactive dispatch).
  • Inputs: command name and arguments.
  • Behavior: logs the command via audit_log unless dockistrate_command_skips_runtime_prep marks it as pre-runtime, applies VISIBILITY_POLICY=redacted to Docker option, header-value, and generic Nginx directive-value audit/verbose copies, then dispatches the original arguments to the appropriate function. Command copies use the same argument classification as review screens and saved-command sensitivity checks, following actual CLI/interactive argument boundaries rather than treating prompt metadata names as options.
  • Side effects: emits verbose output to stderr and triggers command execution.

_run_command_fix_permissions (lib/cli/run_command.sh)

  • Entry points: CLI and interactive fix-permissions dispatch.
  • Behavior: loads deferred command definitions without runtime initialization, then runs permission repair. Direct sourcing falls back to loading only the permission entrypoint when needed.

dockistrate_command_skips_runtime_prep (lib/cli/pre_runtime_commands.sh)

  • Entry points: dockistrate.sh, interactive_picker_run_command_prompt, run_command.
  • Behavior: central predicate for commands that must reach dispatch before runtime prep and audit/config bootstrap side effects: help, help update, help-update, upgrade-preflight, fix-permissions, and restore-backup. Restore performs its own preparation and logging after confirming and validating the candidate.

interactive_picker (lib/cli/interactive_picker.sh)

  • Entry points: interactive mode loop in dockistrate.sh.
  • Behavior: shows a task-oriented home screen for common flows, including adding a backend, recent commands, favorites, port updates, service lifecycle, certificates, security rules, update helpers, diagnostics, global command search, and the advanced command browser. The home prompt includes interactive_dashboard_summary when available. When a command is chosen, it ensures deferred runtime prep has run unless the command is pre-runtime, checks interactive-only state availability with interactive_command_availability, gathers args via prompt_args_for_command, and re-enters that prompt when review-before-run asks to edit previous answers.
  • Interactive notes: recent/favorite reruns reuse review_command_before_run before setting SELECTED_CMD/SELECTED_ARGS; read-only commands bypass review, while mutating and destructive commands keep the same review and confirmation behavior. Global search matches command names, aliases, descriptions, and category names across all interactive categories. The advanced command browser preserves the category menu with focused backend override and global setting groups, while update helpers are also available from the home screen; when launched from home it can return to the home screen without exiting interactive mode. Category-local filtering and special flows for ACL/security rules are preserved. If a selected command requires missing state, command lists annotate the row before selection and the picker still shows guidance with a suggested setup action, return, or quit after selection. Supported menus expose contextual ? help without changing the current selection or filter.

interactive_command_browser (lib/cli/interactive_picker.sh)

  • Entry points: interactive_picker home screen.
  • Behavior: shows the advanced category browser, including the global search entry and all interactive command categories; in direct mode, Quit preserves the previous top-level picker exit behavior, while home-launched mode exposes Back to home and a distinct Quit path.

prompt_args_for_command (lib/cli/prompt_args_for_command.sh)

  • Entry points: interactive picker.
  • Default selection: generic menus initially highlight the matching underlying current/default value without reordering choices or parsing display labels. Keep-current sentinels retain their meaning, including avoiding explicit backend image replacement. An unmatched default keeps the first choice; this initial index is scoped to that chooser and cannot affect the later Run/Cancel review.
  • Cancellation: EOF in generic and specialized interactive menus and text/manual/multiline entry cancels and clears the selection. Enter retains the documented blank/default behavior, including security/ACL and header prompts.
  • Behavior: resets per-prompt dynamic-choice caches, resolves argument specs, renders friendly labels/help/examples through arg_metadata, prompts for values, validates, routes mutating commands through review_command_before_run, and prepares accepted args for run_command.
  • Interactive notes: supports multi-line manual entry for docker_opts, maps Keep current sentinels to current values, supports explicit clear sentinels, preserves the existing pull-mode default for image presets while allowing always|if-missing|never, lets generic multi-argument prompts backtrack to the previous prompted argument, and lets review-before-run return to editing after all arguments are collected. The raw arg spec remains the machine-readable source; labels and examples are display metadata only.
  • Interactive notes: delegates to specialized collectors for add-backend, add-host-alias, and update-port; delegates to header and security handlers for set-hsts, set-csp, set-backend-hsts, set-backend-csp, and add-acl, plus post-processing for path, certificate, and image commands.

collect_add_backend_interactive (lib/cli/collect_add_backend_interactive.sh)

  • Navigation: Back and Esc/Q return to the previous visible question across HTTP, HTTPS redirect choices, TCP and UDP. Back at the first step or EOF at any menu/text prompt cancels and clears the selection. Host-port availability is checked only when exposure is selected; command execution still rechecks availability.
  • Entry points: prompt_args_for_command for add-backend.
  • Behavior: step-by-step wizard for domain, protocol, network, image, ports, certificates, redirect, websocket, exposure, docker opts; HTTPS certificate choices include existing cert directories plus self-signed and Let's Encrypt generation; validates listen-port availability and re-prompts on host port conflicts.
  • Interactive notes: listen and redirect-target ports use common/default/manual picker choices; docker opts input accepts multi-line entry and is normalized before persistence.
  • Side effects: none directly; produces SELECTED_ARGS for add_backend.

collect_add_host_alias_interactive (lib/cli/collect_add_host_alias_interactive.sh)

  • Entry points: prompt_args_for_command for add-host-alias.
  • Behavior: forces backend selection (HTTP/HTTPS only) and validates alias.

collect_update_port_interactive (lib/cli/collect_update_port_interactive.sh)

  • Entry points: prompt_args_for_command for update-port.
  • Behavior: prompts for backend domain, existing port mapping, new listen/container ports, protocol, certificate, WebSocket, HTTP/3, and Alt-Svc using picker choices before review; produces flag-style update-port args so the reviewed CLI equivalent matches the command that will run.
  • Interactive notes: manual entry is retained for custom ports, custom Alt-Svc values, and manual certificate paths; the review screen appears only after the existing mapping and desired values are selected.
  • Side effects: none directly; produces SELECTED_ARGS for update_port_mapping.

get_arg_spec (lib/cli/get_arg_spec.sh)

  • Entry points: prompt_args_for_command.
  • Behavior: returns semicolon-separated name|default specs for each command.

get_arg_choices (lib/cli/get_arg_choices.sh)

  • Entry points: interactive prompts.
  • Behavior: dispatches to __arg_choices_<arg> helpers to produce dynamic menu choices based on current args and state files.
  • Path choices: preserve the entire stored path in both the label and selected argument, including /api|assets and regex alternatives such as /(api|assets). This applies to update/remove-path-option and path-scoped Nginx directive menus. CLI callers pass the same literal path as one shell-quoted argument.
  • Choice encoding: path producers emit quoted CSV value,label rows. The shared decoder recognizes a valid two-field row with a quoted first field before considering legacy value|label rows, so pipes inside a path cannot become menu separators. Legacy image and rule labels still preserve their commas.
  • Host choices: independent headers/policies include ordinary aliases and dedicated hosts. __arg_choices_server_domains includes backends and dedicated hosts for mTLS, HTTP-version and IP-header settings; ordinary aliases inherit these from their backend.
  • Interactive notes: uses Docker to list images/networks when available.

arg_choices_images helpers (lib/cli/arg_choices_images.sh)

  • Entry points: get_arg_choices.
  • Behavior: provides __arg_choices_image, __arg_choices_container_port, __arg_choices_nginx_image, __arg_choices_certbot_image, and pull-mode choices ordered around the selected preset's default.

arg_choices_network_docker helpers (lib/cli/arg_choices_network_docker.sh)

  • Entry points: get_arg_choices.
  • Behavior: provides __arg_choices_network, __arg_choices_docker_opts.

arg_choices_protocols helpers (lib/cli/arg_choices_protocols.sh)

  • Entry points: get_arg_choices.
  • Behavior: provides __arg_choices_protocol, __arg_choices_ws, __arg_choices_listen, __arg_choices_version.

arg_choices_security helpers (lib/cli/arg_choices_security.sh)

  • Entry points: get_arg_choices.
  • Behavior: provides __arg_choices_mode, __arg_choices_allow_or_deny, __arg_choices_policy, __arg_choices_code, __arg_choices_source, __arg_choices_condition.

arg_choices_misc helpers (lib/cli/arg_choices_misc.sh)

  • Entry points: get_arg_choices.

review_command helpers (lib/cli/review_command.sh)

  • Flag-based reviews use option summaries in lib/cli/review_command_options.sh; directive names follow their selected scope.
  • Argument summaries use the final execution layout: path and security-rule flags, proxy startup options, uninstall scope, and scoped directive removal retain meaningful field names. Security-rule conditions are grouped by condition number. Commands without arguments show (none); explicit empty values used to clear options remain real operands in the CLI equivalent and execution. Display-only formatting continues to honor the configured visibility policy.
  • Backend updates: managed and explicit-replacement interactive arguments render as valid CLI flags. Keep-current images omit --image, preserving unchanged-container semantics; explicit image choices still request replacement, and cleared Docker options remain an empty --docker-opts value.
  • Port summaries: add-port parses the postprocessed positional arguments and --http3/--alt-svc options into semantic values. Its displayed CLI equivalent preserves exact argument boundaries. update-port retains its existing dedicated formatter.
  • Entry points: prompt_args_for_command and specialized interactive collectors.
  • Behavior: classifies commands as read-only, mutating, or destructive; formats the equivalent CLI invocation with shell-safe quoting; renders a human-readable argument summary using arg_metadata; applies VISIBILITY_POLICY=redacted to Docker option, header-value, and generic Nginx directive-value display copies; and asks the operator to Run, Edit previous answers, or Cancel before mutating commands execute. The shared classifier protects compact scope-dependent directive values and flag-like text inside sensitive values without changing execution arguments. The specialized add-backend review labels redirect answers and renders flag-based CLI equivalents plus a follow-up redirect command when needed.
  • Interactive notes: read-only commands such as status, status-all, check-config, tail-proxy-logs, list-*, and show-* bypass the review screen. Destructive commands require exact YES confirmation after choosing Run.

Domain configuration review (lib/cli/review_domain_config.sh)

  • Entry points: generic command review, recents/favorites replay, and the specialized security-rule collector.
  • Behavior: Apply and Migrate show their actual dry-run output before the Run confirmation. Commands targeting pending files offer review, apply, or cancellation. A successful pending-file apply returns the refresh/recollect status so the original command cannot run with stale choices; invalid candidates never reach mutation confirmation.

interactive_no_state helpers (lib/cli/interactive_no_state.sh)

  • Entry points: interactive_picker_run_command_prompt.
  • Behavior: detects interactive-only missing-state cases before argument collection, including no backends, no port mappings, no certificates, no backups, no backend headers, no mTLS-enabled backends, no ACL rules, and no security rules.
  • Interactive notes: renders a guidance screen through choose_option with a suggested setup command, return to the previous menu, or quit. Command pickers also reuse the availability result to append short display suffixes such as unavailable: no port mappings. restore-backup uses soft wording when no local backups are listed because the explicit backup-path prompt remains available. This does not change CLI dispatch or non-interactive command behavior.

interactive_dashboard helpers (lib/cli/interactive_dashboard.sh)

  • Entry points: interactive_picker.
  • Behavior: renders a best-effort home dashboard summary with proxy state, backend count, port count, certificate directory count, backup count, and capture state.
  • Interactive notes: state-file counts do not require Docker; proxy and capture state return unknown before deferred runtime prep, when Docker is unavailable, or when Docker cannot be queried. Helpers do not modify state.

interactive_recents helpers (lib/cli/interactive_recents.sh)

  • Entry points: dockistrate.sh interactive loop after successful run_command, interactive_picker home screen.
  • Reads/Writes: state/config/interactive_recent.csv, state/config/interactive_favorites.csv.
  • Behavior: stores successful interactive command selections as CSV-safe rows with timestamp, command, arg count, and nested CSV-encoded args; keeps only the latest 10 recents; preserves operator-entered values in default full mode; loads and displays recent/favorite commands for rerun. Redacted mode skips recording/favoriting commands with Docker option, header, or generic Nginx directive values and omits existing affected entries from the picker using the shared command argument classifier. Malformed saved argument payloads are skipped in either mode and rejected when adding favorites. Leading empty argument fields are preserved when serializing; CSV format is unchanged and no schema migration is needed. Saved files and replacement files require owner-only access; a private-access failure prevents reading or persisting their contents. Existing malformed rows are not repaired or deleted, and policy changes/removal of active settings do not purge history. The recent count limit and explicit favorite removal remain unchanged; neither file has age-based expiry.
  • Interactive notes: recent and favorite reruns call review_command_before_run before selection and share command-specific verbose/preparation handling; replayed permission repairs skip runtime initialization and log capture, while restores defer them until candidate validation. Read-only commands rerun without review; mutating commands show the review screen, and destructive commands keep exact-confirmation behavior. Recent entries can be added to or removed from favorites from the saved-command action menu.

_interactive_prepare_saved_file (lib/cli/interactive_recents.sh)

  • Entry points: saved-command load, record, favorite lookup/add/remove.
  • Behavior: validates runtime paths, creates a missing file under a private umask, requires regular unlinked owner-only storage, then initializes or validates its CSV header before reading arguments. A failed initialization can leave an empty private file; no command values have been written at that point.

_interactive_finalize_saved_file (lib/cli/interactive_recents.sh)

  • Entry points: recent/favorite replacement.
  • Behavior: rechecks private target access, publishes the prepared CSV atomically with mode 600, and removes its temporary replacement if finalization fails.

upgrade_preflight (lib/cli/upgrade_preflight.sh)

  • Entry points: CLI and interactive upgrade-preflight.
  • Behavior: read-only compatibility check for current on-disk state and optional local release tag. It validates the current schema marker, reports backup presence, warns when persisted security rules use operators whose generated behavior was corrected to match documented condition semantics; each rule action determines rejection behavior, optionally enforces --require-backup, validates stable local tags via refs/tags/<tag>, reads target VERSION and schema metadata through git -C "$SCRIPT_DIR" show, requires the tag name to match the target VERSION, and fails downgrades with cannot downgrade state from N to M.
  • Reads/Writes: reads state/config/state_schema_version, SECURITY_RULES_DB, direct children of state/backups/, bounded backup archive member listings, and local git tag metadata. Writes nothing.
  • Side effects: none; no Docker checks, runtime bootstrap, audit logging, migrations, config repair, remote fetch, or update application.

upgrade_preflight helpers (lib/cli/upgrade_preflight.sh)

  • Entry points: upgrade_preflight.
  • Behavior: includes upgrade_preflight_usage, upgrade_preflight_error_usage, upgrade_preflight_validate_tag, upgrade_preflight_validate_version, upgrade_preflight_git_has_local_tag, upgrade_preflight_git_show_file, upgrade_preflight_parse_schema_constant, upgrade_preflight_read_target_version, upgrade_preflight_read_target_schema, upgrade_preflight_check_tag_version_match, upgrade_preflight_backup_exists, upgrade_preflight_backup_archive_is_full, upgrade_preflight_backup_archive_validate_listing, upgrade_preflight_check_backup, upgrade_preflight_compare_schema, and upgrade_preflight_parse_args. Backup archive inspection streams tar -tzf output through bounded entry-count and entry-length validation while requiring all members to stay under the archive root and include config/. Historical tag shell is parsed as text only; legacy common.sh fallback accepts exactly CURRENT_STATE_SCHEMA_VERSION="N" with N > 0.
