Module: backends (lib/backends/*.sh)

add_backend (lib/backends/add_backend.sh)

  • Entry points: CLI add-backend; interactive wizard -> run_command.
  • Inputs: domain, image, container_port, protocol, and optional --listen, --cert selfsigned|letsencrypt|none|path, --ws, --docker-opts, --network, --expose.
  • Behavior: validates inputs, normalizes domain, ensures no alias collision, determines listen port defaults, preflights host-port availability for newly introduced listeners, handles HTTPS certificate selection (none and selfsigned mint self-signed certs; letsencrypt reuses the Certbot add-cert flow), enforces certificate directory containment under state/certs, normalizes docker options to canonical single-line storage, ensures network, starts and verifies a container with reserved ownership labels, saves its full ID and launch token, writes backend and port records (the mock test mode uses a 127.0.0.1 placeholder IP), and optionally adds HTTP redirect for HTTPS. Registers recovery before launching Docker; failed starts and later transaction failures remove only launch-owned containers by immutable ID, preserving unrelated same-name containers and reporting incomplete runtime recovery.
  • Reads/Writes: BACKEND_PORTS_FILE, state/config/backend_identity.csv, BACKEND_DOCKER_OPTS_FILE, certificate directories.
  • Side effects: docker run, new config entries, backups, update_nginx_config.
  • Interactive notes: uses positional args from wizard and can prompt for certificate paths and redirect.

update_backend (lib/backends/update_backend.sh)

  • Entry points: CLI update-backend; interactive prompts.
  • Inputs: domain plus --image, --container-port, --docker-opts, --network; explicit identity upgrade adds --replace-unmanaged-container <full-id> and requires --image.
  • Behavior: resolves alias, verifies the saved container ID and ownership, loads current backend entry, normalizes docker options to canonical storage before use, optionally recreates container when image or docker opts change, updates network attachments (including hyphenated network names), updates stored IP/port, and updates port mappings if container port changes. Recreate flows stage the original container by immutable identity, preserve anonymous volumes, and retain it until the configuration transaction commits. Failed starts and later failures remove only launch-owned replacement containers and restore the original container's name and running state; unrelated same-name containers are preserved and incomplete runtime recovery is reported. Network-change flows track runtime mutations and restore container network attachments during rollback when a downstream failure occurs.
  • Reads/Writes: BACKEND_PORTS_FILE, state/config/backend_identity.csv, BACKEND_DOCKER_OPTS_FILE.
  • Side effects: may docker rename, docker rm -f, docker run, docker network connect, backup transaction, update_nginx_config.
  • Interactive notes: blank docker opts means keep current; explicit clear selection removes stored docker opts; avoids restart unless changed.
  • Stopped backends: replacement preserves the declared stopped state and creates the new container without starting it. Network changes also preserve stopped state and update the actual attachment even when Docker reports no assigned IP. A failed disconnect with the old attachment still present fails and triggers rollback. Both CLI and interactive updates use these checks. Use start-backend to start it explicitly.
  • Identity upgrade: --replace-unmanaged-container <full-id> plus explicit --image authorizes a controlled replacement only for a configured backend without a saved identity. Verifies the supplied full ID and expected name before staging it; the new container receives full labels and transactional identity. CLI and interactive flows support it. Other identity-less backend rows retain saved routing only within this explicit upgrade; ordinary refresh stays strict. See upgrade procedure.
  • Application preservation: replacement does not transfer writable-layer data. Saved bind/volume options remain unless explicitly changed. Operator-managed files such as apps/<domain>/public/ are ignored by Git and require separate application backups; Dockistrate backups cover managed state. Each replacement commits independently and removes its original container after commit.

replace_backend_network (lib/backends/replace_backend_network.sh)

  • Entry points: CLI replace-backend-network; interactive picker.
  • Behavior: wrapper over update_backend --network, including stopped-state preservation, membership verification without requiring an IP, and network rollback on failure.

remove_backend (lib/backends/remove_backend.sh)

  • Entry points: CLI remove-backend [--yes] <domain>.
  • Completion reporting: CLI and interactive flows report the removed container only after its committed deletion succeeds.
  • Behavior: resolves alias, prompts before removing an existing backend container in interactive mode, and aborts the whole command if that confirmation is declined. Non-interactive removal without --yes remains compatible but emits an auto-confirm warning; --yes makes scripted confirmation explicit. When removal proceeds, Dockistrate first cleans related config entries, path headers, TLS overrides, ACL/security rule overrides, alias mappings, and mTLS material, then removes the backend container with attached anonymous volumes only after update_nginx_config succeeds. Persisted mTLS state is validated under the transaction lock and cleanup is limited to the exact non-symlink direct child owned by the removed domain. If the mTLS root is truly absent, an exact canonical stale mapping can be removed from state without recreating the root; unsafe mappings still fail atomically. Other destructive file/dir deletes are constrained to expected state roots via safe-delete guards.
  • Dependent hosts: captures aliases and dedicated hosts under the mutation lock, removes their domain-keyed policies, owned mTLS material, and assembled/per-domain ACL includes after removing the host mappings, and preserves any surviving colliding identity. Canonical owned mTLS directories are cleaned even when mTLS was previously disabled; inherited parent trust is never selected for deletion. Shared server certificate owners remain as certificate-only domains; unrelated hosts retain their settings. Transactions restore material and generated includes if removal or final publication fails.
  • Reads/Writes: multiple backend config files, BACKEND_PORTS_FILE, SECURITY_RULES_DB, SECURITY_IP_RULES_DB.
  • Side effects: removes Docker container and attached anonymous volumes after config update success, deletes include files, backups, update_nginx_config.

_remove_backend_remove_alias_render_state (lib/backends/remove_backend.sh)

  • Entry points: remove_backend after ordinary alias mappings are removed.
  • Behavior: removes domain-keyed render settings for a captured alias only when that hostname no longer identifies a backend, dedicated host, or surviving alias. The shared removal helper then cleans its owned artifacts; server certificate material is preserved.

_removed_identity_mtls_target (lib/backends/removal_cleanup.sh)

  • Entry points: backend removal, dedicated-host removal and clean-all before state writes.
  • Behavior: validates explicit mTLS ownership, or the canonical owned directory when mTLS is disabled. Never resolves inherited trust. Missing paths are retained as transaction targets so material appearing after preflight is rechecked during cleanup.

_removed_identity_cleanup_artifacts (lib/backends/removal_cleanup.sh)

  • Entry points: explicit backend removal, dedicated-host removal and clean-all after hostname mappings are removed.
  • Behavior: preserves surviving colliding identities, revalidates owned mTLS paths, and removes only that identity's authority material and HTTP/stream ACL includes and mirrors. Server certificate material is preserved.

remove_all_backends (lib/backends/remove_all_backends.sh)

  • Entry points: CLI and interactive remove-all-backends.
  • Behavior: collects sorted unique backend domains before calling remove_backend, preserving caller input for each interactive confirmation. Declined removals leave the backend intact and continue to the next domain; the summary counts only removed backends. Non-interactive automatic confirmation is unchanged.
  • Side effects: removes backend containers/config via remove_backend, creates a backup when removals occur.

start_backend (lib/backends/start_backend.sh)

  • Entry points: CLI and interactive start-backend.
  • Behavior: verifies the backend identity and starts that full container ID; a same-name foreign container is never used.
  • Domain state: publishes the declared running state and requests a finalized automatic backup even when the address remains unchanged.
  • Side effects: docker start, backup entry.

stop_backend (lib/backends/stop_backend.sh)

  • Entry points: CLI and interactive stop-backend.
  • Behavior: verifies the backend identity and stops that full container ID.
  • Domain state: publishes the declared stopped state and requests a finalized automatic backup; failed snapshot creation rolls back the operation.
  • Side effects: docker stop, backup entry.

restart_backend (lib/backends/restart_backend.sh)

  • Entry points: CLI and interactive restart-backend.
  • Behavior: verifies the backend identity and restarts that full container ID.
  • Domain state: requests the same finalized automatic backup as start/stop; unchanged snapshot contents may reuse the existing backup.
  • Side effects: docker restart, backup entry.

start_all_backends (lib/backends/start_all_backends.sh)

  • Entry points: CLI start-all-backends.
  • Behavior: verifies all configured backend identities before starting any by full ID, updates nginx (refreshes backend IPs during the update).
  • Side effects: docker start for each container, update_nginx_config, backup entry.

stop_all_backends (lib/backends/stop_all_backends.sh)

  • Entry points: CLI stop-all-backends.
  • Behavior: verifies all configured backend identities before stopping any by full ID.
  • Side effects: docker stop for each container, backup entry.

restart_all_backends (lib/backends/restart_all_backends.sh)

  • Entry points: CLI restart-all-backends.
  • Behavior: verifies all configured backend identities before restarting any by full ID, updates nginx (refreshes backend IPs during the update).
  • Side effects: docker restart for each container, update_nginx_config, backup entry.

list_backends (lib/backends/list_backends.sh)

  • Entry points: CLI list-backends, status, status-all.
  • Behavior: prints backend table with aliases, images, networks, overrides, and port summary. Runtime status and image come only from a verified container ID. A proven absent saved ID is missing; unproven ownership or a failed Docker query is unverified, without trusting a same-name replacement.

list_host_aliases (lib/backends/list_host_aliases.sh)

  • Entry points: CLI list-host-aliases.
  • Behavior: prints alias -> backend mappings (optionally filtered by domain).

add_host_alias (lib/backends/add_host_alias.sh)

  • Entry points: CLI add-host-alias; interactive wizard.
  • Behavior: validates alias and backend, ensures backend has an HTTP/HTTPS port mapping, writes alias mapping.
  • Side effects: writes backend_aliases.csv, backups, nginx update.

remove_host_alias (lib/backends/remove_host_alias.sh)

  • Entry points: CLI remove-host-alias.
  • Behavior: removes the alias and its keyed render state and ACL includes transactionally, preserving state belonging to colliding backend or dedicated-host identities. Recreating a name does not revive old alias policy.
  • Side effects: updates backend_aliases.csv and keyed settings, backups, security-effective proxy replacement in CLI and interactive mode; interrupts active sessions.

remove_dedicated_host (lib/backends/remove_dedicated_host.sh)

  • Entry points: CLI and interactive remove-dedicated-host <hostname>.
  • Behavior: removes the association, inheritance and keyed policies, owned mTLS material (including previously disabled material), and assembled/per-domain ACL includes. Inherited parent trust, shared server certificates and surviving colliding identities are preserved. Ownership checks precede writes; standalone transactions include owned material and generated files so failures restore them.

set_dedicated_host_inherit (lib/backends/set_dedicated_host_inherit.sh)

  • Entry points: CLI and interactive set-dedicated-host-inherit.
  • Behavior: updates the selected inheritance setting transactionally. acl, security_rules, headers, and all replace the managed proxy and check config readiness so connections authorized by previous rules or client identity do not survive; mtls and paths retain their existing update path.
  • Compatibility: security-effective inheritance changes now interrupt active proxy sessions compared with 1.0.1; syntax and state formats are unchanged.

_backend_container_snapshot (lib/backends/identity.sh)

  • Entry points: backend refresh, lifecycle, update, status, capture and cleanup.
  • Behavior: loads one strict saved identity record and inspects that full ID once. Verifies managed role, physical state root, normalized domain and launch token before exposing status, image or network/IP fields. Missing/duplicate/malformed identity, mismatched labels and uncertain inspection fail closed.

_backend_snapshot_has_network (lib/backends/identity.sh)

  • Entry points: update_backend network changes, including replace-backend-network and domain apply.
  • Behavior: checks exact network membership in the verified snapshot independently of IP assignment. Rejects an empty network name; performs no Docker calls or state writes.

_backend_cleanup_snapshot (lib/backends/identity.sh)

  • Entry points: backend removal, clean-all, uninstall-all.
  • Behavior: accepts a verified backend snapshot or a definitively absent saved ID with no container occupying the expected name. Otherwise fails before state deletion. Cleanup and rollback retain the verified ID/token independently of the removed identity file.

backend_has_httpish_port (lib/backends/common.sh)

  • Entry points: alias validation.
  • Behavior: checks whether domain has HTTP/HTTPS port mapping.

get_backend_port (lib/backends/common.sh)

  • Entry points: CLI prompts and updates.
  • Behavior: returns backend container port from BACKEND_PORTS_FILE.

get_backend_image (lib/backends/common.sh)

  • Entry points: CLI prompts and status.
  • Behavior: reads the configured image from the verified backend container snapshot; missing or mismatched identity fails.

get_backend_network (lib/backends/common.sh)

  • Entry points: CLI prompts and update.
  • Behavior: returns stored network or default.

get_backend_docker_opts (lib/backends/common.sh)

  • Entry points: interactive prompts.
  • Behavior: reads docker opts from BACKEND_DOCKER_OPTS_FILE without collapsing internal whitespace.

set_backend_docker_opts (lib/backends/common.sh)

  • Entry points: add_backend, update_backend, remove_backend.
  • Behavior: stores or clears docker opts for a backend and strips CR/LF before persistence so state remains single-line.

_parse_docker_opts_to_lines (lib/backends/_parse_docker_opts_to_lines.sh)

  • Entry points: backend create/update and nginx docker-opts validation/runtime assembly.
  • Behavior: parses a shell-like string of docker args into tokens (handles quotes/escapes), including docs-style line continuations (\ + newline/CRLF), and preserves inner quotes for compact JSON env assignments such as KEY=["a"] or KEY={"a":"b"}.

_docker_opts_normalize_profile (lib/backends/validate_docker_opts.sh)

  • Entry points: normalize_docker_opts_for_storage.
  • Behavior: normalizes the docker-opts guardrail profile to backend or nginx (defaults to backend).

_docker_opts_conflicting_option_key (lib/backends/validate_docker_opts.sh)

  • Entry points: normalize_docker_opts_for_storage.
  • Behavior: maps tokens (including bundled short options and --opt=value forms) to blocked option keys for the active profile without interpreting attached option values as more flags. A terminal value-taking shorthand in a boolean bundle may still consume the following token.

_docker_opts_conflict_owner_guidance (lib/backends/validate_docker_opts.sh)

  • Entry points: normalize_docker_opts_for_storage.
  • Behavior: returns owner-guidance text for rejected docker flags so errors point to the Dockistrate command that controls that concern.

_docker_opts_option_arity (lib/backends/validate_docker_opts.sh)

  • Entry points: Docker option validation and shorthand-bundle helpers.
  • Behavior: classifies recognized Docker run flags as boolean or value-taking, and returns unknown for other flags. Covers long options, hidden aliases, platform-specific options, and known shorthands without depending on the installed Docker client.

_docker_opts_validate_option_token (lib/backends/validate_docker_opts.sh)

  • Entry points: normalize_docker_opts_for_storage.
  • Behavior: requires explicit values for unknown long options and rejects unknown shorthand characters. Stops interpreting a shorthand bundle at a value-taking flag or a boolean's explicit =value; respects redacted output when reporting rejected option names.

normalize_docker_opts_for_storage (lib/backends/validate_docker_opts.sh)

  • Entry points: backend add/update, start_nginx, set_nginx_docker_opts, and nginx runtime preflight in recreate_nginx_container.
  • Inputs: raw docker opts string, context label, optional profile (backend|nginx).
  • Behavior: tokenizes docker opts, rejects control characters, applies profile-based guardrails, rejects positional image/command tokens plus -- end-of-options marker that can override Dockistrate-managed runtime assembly, rejects options that are missing required values, rejects nginx-profile labels under com.dockistrate.* and the five backend ownership labels, preserves quotes in compact JSON env assignments, and returns canonical single-line shell-quoted storage.
  • Option arity: uses an explicit Docker run boolean/value table, including --use-api-socket and --disable-content-trust. Unknown long options require --option=value (or =true/=false for booleans); unknown short flags are rejected. Boolean shorthand prefixes stop at an explicit =, and value-taking shorthands own the remaining suffix or the next token. Option-shaped values use explicit = syntax.
  • Runtime safety: shared by CLI and interactive flows; backend creation validates options before transaction/certificate work, and updates validate selected or saved options before starting a transaction or creating the target network. Saved proxy options are revalidated and tokenized before preparing state, pulling an image, or removing the existing proxy during direct recreation.
  • Guardrails:
    • backend: rejects --name, --network/--net, --rm, and direct labels for com.dockistrate.managed, .role, .state-dir, .backend-domain, .backend-launch; other labels and label files remain supported.
    • nginx: rejects --name, --network/--net, -p/--publish, -P/--publish-all, -v/--volume, --mount, --entrypoint, --rm.

resolve_backend_domain (lib/backends/common.sh)

  • Entry points: most backend/port commands.
  • Behavior: resolves aliases to primary domains and can log info.

refresh_backend_ips (lib/backends/common.sh)

  • Entry points: nginx update.
  • Behavior: updates stored IPs only from snapshots of saved immutable IDs with matching ownership. Builds the complete replacement before writing, so one invalid identity leaves all rows unchanged; no-op when SKIP_DOCKER_CHECKS=true.
  • Side effects: updates BACKEND_PORTS_FILE, backups when changes occur.

refresh_backend_networks (lib/backends/common.sh)

  • Entry points: nginx update.
  • Behavior: refreshes network and IP together from one verified snapshot per backend, preferring the configured network. Refuses unowned replacements or missing usable IPv4 addresses without replacing state. During explicit legacy replacement only, other identity-less rows retain saved routing with a warning; no runtime discovery occurs for them. No-op when SKIP_DOCKER_CHECKS=true.
  • Side effects: updates BACKEND_PORTS_FILE, backups when changes occur.

summarize_container_image (lib/backends/common.sh)

  • Entry points: status displays.
  • Behavior: prints a concise image reference for a running container.

Module: ports (lib/ports/*.sh)

add_port_mapping (lib/ports/add_port_mapping.sh)

  • Entry points: CLI add-port.
  • Inputs: domain, nginx_port, container_port, protocol (http|https|tcp|udp), cert_path, ws, optional http3/alt-svc flags.
  • Behavior: validates inputs, ensures backend exists, skips duplicates before certificate creation, preflights host-port availability for newly introduced listeners, handles HTTPS certificate creation/validation under state/certs, enforces transport-aware listener uniqueness, appends port record.
  • Side effects: writes BACKEND_PORTS_FILE, creates a certificate if needed, backups, update_nginx_config.

update_port_mapping (lib/ports/update_port_mapping.sh)

  • Entry points: CLI update-port.
  • Behavior: selects existing mapping, checks for duplicate target port before certificate creation, preflights host-port availability when moving a listener to a new host port, updates port/protocol/cert/ws/http3/alt-svc with certificate directories constrained to state/certs, updates path overrides if port changes, clears redirects when non-HTTP.
  • Interactive notes: picker-driven calls pass flag-style args and run directly after review; the legacy raw prompt path is retained only for direct interactive calls without update flags.
  • Side effects: edits BACKEND_PORTS_FILE, may create a certificate (suppresses nested nginx updates), backups, update_nginx_config.

remove_port_mapping (lib/ports/remove_port_mapping.sh)

  • Entry points: CLI remove-port.
  • Behavior: removes port mapping and related path overrides; removes TLS overrides if needed.
  • Side effects: edits BACKEND_PORTS_FILE, TLS override files, backups, update_nginx_config.

list_port_mappings (lib/ports/list_port_mappings.sh)

  • Entry points: CLI list-port-mappings, status, status-all.
  • Behavior: prints human-readable port mappings including transport (http|https|tcp|udp) and HTTPS HTTP/3 state.

set_port_redirect (lib/ports/set_port_redirect.sh)

  • Entry points: CLI set-port-redirect.
  • Inputs: domain, port, on|off (legacy yes|no remains accepted), status code (with optional target port).
  • Behavior: validates the HTTP port mapping, canonicalizes legacy redirect aliases, and stores the redirect flag as on|off with its code.
  • Side effects: edits BACKEND_PORTS_FILE, backups, update_nginx_config.

remove_port_redirect (lib/ports/remove_port_redirect.sh)

  • Entry points: CLI remove-port-redirect.
  • Behavior: clears redirect flag and code.
  • Side effects: updates BACKEND_PORTS_FILE, backups, update_nginx_config.

set_port_http3 (lib/ports/port_http3.sh)

  • Entry points: CLI set-port-http3.
  • Inputs: HTTPS listen port, on|off, optional Alt-Svc mode/value.
  • Behavior: rewrites HTTPS port rows to update http3 and alt_svc state, then regenerates nginx config.
  • Side effects: updates BACKEND_PORTS_FILE, backups, update_nginx_config.

list_port_http3 (lib/ports/port_http3.sh)

  • Entry points: CLI list-port-http3.
  • Behavior: lists deduplicated HTTPS port HTTP/3 and Alt-Svc state.

enable_ws (lib/ports/enable_ws.sh)

  • Entry points: CLI enable-ws.
  • Behavior: delegates to _set_ws_flag with yes.

disable_ws (lib/ports/disable_ws.sh)

  • Entry points: CLI disable-ws.
  • Behavior: delegates to _set_ws_flag with no.

_set_ws_flag (lib/ports/common.sh)

  • Entry points: WS enable/disable.
  • Behavior: updates ws flag in port record; validates port.
  • Side effects: updates BACKEND_PORTS_FILE, backups, update_nginx_config.

get_backend_ws_flag (lib/ports/common.sh)

  • Entry points: nginx config generation.
  • Behavior: returns ws flag for a domain and port from the port record.

add_path_option (lib/ports/add_path_option.sh)

  • Entry points: CLI add-path-option.
  • Inputs: domain, nginx_port, path_prefix, optional ws/redirect/headers plus match/priority/target/rewrite/reason/loc.
  • Behavior: validates path, ensures a compatible port mapping exists, parses path routing options and metadata, stores path record.
  • Side effects: updates BACKEND_PORTS_FILE, backups, update_nginx_config.

update_path_option (lib/ports/update_path_option.sh)

  • Entry points: CLI and interactive update-path-option.
  • Behavior: updates path override attributes (including advanced routing fields), validates, prevents duplicates.
  • Side effects: updates BACKEND_PORTS_FILE, backups, update_nginx_config.

remove_path_option (lib/ports/remove_path_option.sh)

  • Entry points: CLI and interactive remove-path-option.
  • Behavior: deletes the exact domain/listener/literal-path record and its managed/raw Nginx directives, including matching dedicated-host overrides even when path inheritance is disabled. Other path targets and non-path directive scopes are preserved.
  • Side effects: transactionally updates BACKEND_PORTS_FILE and NGINX_DIRECTIVES_FILE, requests a backup and update_nginx_config, and publishes editable/applied domain state. Cleanup or activation failures roll back; pending drafts remain protected.

remove_all_path_options (lib/ports/remove_all_path_options.sh)

  • Entry points: CLI and interactive remove-all-path-options.
  • Behavior: removes all path overrides (optionally for a single backend), including paths with no header set, and prunes path header includes. Removes managed/raw path directives for the selected backend and its dedicated hosts, or all path directives when no domain is selected. Non-path scopes are preserved.
  • Side effects: transactionally updates BACKEND_PORTS_FILE, NGINX_DIRECTIVES_FILE, and path header includes, requests a backup and update_nginx_config, and publishes editable/applied domain state. Cleanup or activation failures roll back; pending drafts remain protected.

list_path_options (lib/ports/list_path_options.sh)

  • Entry points: CLI list-path-options, status-all.
  • Behavior: lists path overrides with ws/redirect/header settings and advanced routing metadata.
  • Redirect display: on(inherit) means the path explicitly enables redirection and inherits the listener's code and target port, falling back to 301. inherit also follows the listener's enabled state; explicit codes retain the on(code) display.

_tcp_listen_in_use (lib/ports/common.sh)

  • Entry points: add_backend and port mapping operations.
  • Behavior: checks for an existing TCP port mapping on a given port.

_require_port_mapping_for_path (lib/ports/common.sh)

  • Entry points: path option handlers.
  • Behavior: ensures port mapping exists and is not TCP.

_parse_path_ws (lib/ports/common.sh)

  • Entry points: path option handlers.
  • Behavior: validates yes|no|inherit and sets PATH_WS_FLAG.

_parse_path_redirect (lib/ports/common.sh)

  • Entry points: path option handlers.
  • Behavior: validates redirect settings and sets PATH_REDIRECT_FLAG/PATH_REDIRECT_CODE.

_sanitize_path_for_id (lib/ports/common.sh)

  • Entry points: backups for path overrides.
  • Behavior: sanitizes path into an ID-safe string.

is_valid_path_prefix (lib/ports/common.sh)

  • Entry points: path option validation.
  • Behavior: validates path prefix syntax and rejects Nginx-control characters (#, ;, {, }, control chars).

is_valid_header_set_name (lib/ports/common.sh)

  • Entry points: path header set validation.
  • Behavior: validates header set names for path includes.

Module: nginx (lib/nginx/*.sh)

Proxy runtime updates prepare an allowlisted certificate snapshot with Bash 3,

OpenSSL and standard filesystem tools. Only configured server certificate/key pairs

and public mTLS CA/CRL files are mounted at /etc/letsencrypt; host issuance and

client credentials stay outside default proxy mounts. Snapshots live under

state/config/proxy_certs, outside the mounted Nginx config directory. Both CLI

and interactive workflows replace an older broad mount or changed snapshot;

this interrupts sessions. See certificate isolation and upgrades.

start_nginx (lib/nginx/start_nginx.sh)

  • Entry points: CLI start-nginx.
  • Inputs: optional --nginx-image <image-ref> (name, tag or digest) and optional --docker-opts <opts> ('' clears saved opts).
  • Behavior: validates optional image override, validates/normalizes optional nginx docker opts with nginx-profile guardrails (including rejection of reserved com.dockistrate.* labels), persists changed values to global_settings.csv, rebuilds nginx config, and recreates nginx when image or saved nginx docker opts change on an existing container.
  • Side effects: writes GLOBAL_SETTINGS_FILE, writes nginx config, may recreate container.

recreate_nginx_container (lib/nginx/recreate_nginx_container.sh)

  • Entry points: start_nginx, update_nginx_config, image changes.
  • Behavior: validates the image reference before Docker inspection or replacement, normalizes image ref, validates/parses persisted NGINX_DOCKER_OPTS with nginx-profile guardrails, rejects reserved Dockistrate labels from saved state, computes mapped ports, preflights newly required host ports before container replacement, ensures default network and certificate/webroot directories, prepares a complete allowlisted certificate snapshot before removing the old proxy, builds and mounts the TLS keylog helper before container replacement when decrypt mode is enabled, removes existing container, runs nginx with user-specified docker opts plus Dockistrate-managed labels/mounts/ports/network/image args, connects to backend networks, and reapplies TLS keylog file/dir permissions when decrypt mode is enabled.
  • Side effects: docker rm -f -v, docker run, network connects, may docker pull, creates directories.

_nginx_prepare_certificate_projection (lib/nginx/certificate_projection.sh)

  • Entry points: proxy configuration updates and container recreation.
  • Behavior: validates certificate and mTLS state, selects configured server certificate/key pairs and public CA/CRL files, and builds or verifies an immutable snapshot through Bash filesystem workers. Verified open handles and private staging preserve the selected objects; repeated reads verify source bytes before public PEM extraction. Certbot links must resolve within the certificate root. The snapshot excludes issuance and client private material; the original host paths remain unchanged.
  • Side effects: creates a private CONFIG_DIR/proxy_certs cache owned by the invoking operator and returns a verified generation path. Original server-key ownership is preserved separately. Runtime updates reuse that exact generation for launch and verify the mounted source before retiring old generations within the config transaction.
  • Recovery: transactions that can replay the mounted cache retain its verified manifest and identity before writes. Recovery checks restored snapshot bytes against that captured manifest and restores original metadata without relying on current issuer files. Forward reloads also arm runtime recovery; proxy recovery runs after backend recovery.

ensure_sslkeylog_library (lib/nginx/ensure_sslkeylog_library.sh)

  • Entry points: recreate_nginx_container when TLS decrypt capture is enabled.
  • Behavior: builds the helper inside the configured Nginx image before replacing the proxy. Reuses a cached library only when the image identity and source SHA-256 match; rejects source changes during a build. A failed build leaves no reusable metadata.
  • Side effects: may run a temporary build container and replace the cached library and build metadata under state/tmp/sslkeyloglib.

_sslkeylog_source_fingerprint (lib/nginx/ensure_sslkeylog_library.sh)

  • Entry points: helper build caching, proxy recreation, and existing TLS session validation.
  • Behavior: computes and validates the source SHA-256 using GNU, BSD/macOS, or OpenSSL checksum tools. The digest identifies the helper revision internally; it is not an operator setting.
  • Side effects: none.

reload_nginx_if_running (lib/nginx/common.sh)

  • Entry points: server tokens, config updates.
  • Behavior: runs nginx -s reload in the container if running and returns non-zero on reload failure.

create_nginx_config (lib/nginx/create_nginx_config.sh)

  • Entry points: startup, log field changes.
  • Behavior: runs fix_default_config and cleanup_leftovers, ensures stream dir exists, touches security_rules.inc, creates nginx.conf with log_format from access log fields.
  • Side effects: writes nginx.conf, creates include dirs and placeholder files.

update_nginx_config (lib/nginx/update_nginx_config.sh)

  • Entry points: most configuration changes.
  • Behavior: no-ops when SKIP_UPDATE_NGINX_CONFIG=true; otherwise validates global settings, backend setting overrides, and inheritance before transactions, writes, or Docker work; fail-closes on invalid/tampered backend_ports.csv rows (backend/port/path row validation with line-numbered errors) and invalid mTLS owner mappings before rendering, regenerates nginx configs, builds security includes, updates backend IPs and networks together from one verified snapshot per persisted container ID (unless SKIP_DOCKER_CHECKS=true), refusing unowned replacements before writing generated config, writes HTTP and stream server blocks, recreates nginx container if port set changes, a security update requests replacement, or the selected certificate snapshot differs from the current mount; reloads nginx only when the container is reused.
  • Side effects: writes config files, may recreate nginx container or reload nginx, may rollback on failure; skips container changes when SKIP_DOCKER_CHECKS=true.
  • Security completion: forced replacement removes previous workers and their connections, then checks that the managed replacement is running and nginx -t succeeds. This validates config but does not guarantee every listener/backend is immediately available. CLI and interactive identity/inheritance updates use the same boundary; unlike 1.0.1, they interrupt sessions. No command syntax or saved-state migration is required.

_emit_backend_server_block (lib/nginx/_emit_backend_server_block.sh)

  • Entry points: update_nginx_config for each HTTP/HTTPS mapping.
  • Behavior: uses primary backend settings for both the primary block and ordinary aliases with explicit ACLs. Served names, ACL includes and request-rule identity vary; TLS/mTLS, real-IP, paths, directives and existing Host-based outbound header identity are preserved. Plain aliases remain grouped with the primary.
  • Compatibility: previously stored alias ACLs now take effect during config updates; see alias ACL upgrade behavior.

fix_default_config (lib/nginx/fix_default_config.sh)

  • Entry points: startup and update flows.
  • Behavior: ensures a default self-signed certificate and default server blocks for 80/443 and other mapped ports.
  • Side effects: writes default.conf, generates default certificate files.

normalize_nginx_image (lib/nginx/common.sh)

  • Entry points: image setters, start_nginx.
  • Behavior: appends :latest if no tag/digest provided.

get_all_mapped_ports (lib/nginx/common.sh)

  • Entry points: nginx container creation.
  • Behavior: returns unique mapped ports from BACKEND_PORTS_FILE.

add_nginx_networks (lib/nginx/common.sh)

  • Entry points: after container creation or config update.
  • Behavior: connects nginx container to all backend networks.

remove_unused_nginx_networks (lib/nginx/remove_unused_nginx_networks.sh)

  • Entry points: after config update.
  • Behavior: disconnects nginx from networks no longer used.

stop_nginx (lib/nginx/stop_nginx.sh)

  • Entry points: CLI stop-nginx.
  • Behavior: stops nginx container if running.

remove_nginx (lib/nginx/remove_nginx.sh)

  • Entry points: CLI remove-nginx.
  • Behavior: removes nginx container and attached anonymous volumes.

status (lib/nginx/status.sh)

  • Entry points: CLI status.
  • Behavior: prints the default operator dashboard: proxy status, global settings (including packet capture, TLS-decrypt state, and backup posture), headers, TLS overrides, nginx directive overrides (including strict mode), backend summary with runtime state, ACLs, and container metrics; warns when configured mapped ports differ from runtime published ports; detailed container table lists all Docker containers on the host. In interactive mode, R refreshes the view and Enter returns to the picker.
  • Side effects: reads Docker stats and config files.

status_all (lib/nginx/status.sh)

  • Entry points: CLI status-all.
  • Behavior: extends status with server tokens, access log fields, backend Docker opts, path options, and certificate inventory. In interactive mode, R refreshes the view and Enter returns to the picker.
  • Side effects: reads Docker stats and config files.

get_stats (lib/nginx/common.sh)

  • Entry points: status, status-all.
  • Behavior: returns docker stats info in a pipe-delimited format.

get_sizes (lib/nginx/common.sh)

  • Entry points: status, status-all.
  • Behavior: returns container size information.

tail_proxy_logs (lib/nginx/tail_proxy_logs.sh)

  • Entry points: CLI tail-proxy-logs.
  • Behavior: docker logs -f tailing from nginx container.

describe_image_with_local_state (lib/nginx/describe_image_with_local_state.sh)

  • Entry points: status.
  • Behavior: shows the configured reference, distinguishes mutable tags from digest-pinned content, and describes explicit-pull behavior and local availability. A local tag or digest is observational metadata, not publisher authentication.

_emit_path_locations (lib/nginx/_emit_path_locations.sh)

  • Entry points: config generation.
  • Behavior: emits location blocks for path overrides, computes effective ws and redirect settings.

_write_location_block (lib/nginx/_write_location_block.sh)

  • Entry points: config generation.
  • Behavior: writes a location block with proxy settings, headers, and optional redirect.

_backend_mtls_directives (lib/nginx/_backend_mtls_directives.sh)

  • Entry points: HTTPS server blocks.
  • Behavior: resolves and owner-validates explicit or inherited mTLS state, then emits directives if backend mTLS is enabled. The unchanged /etc/letsencrypt/mtls/<owner>/ca.crt and ca.crl paths refer to public verification files in the proxy snapshot; CA and client private material is not projected.

_ensure_path_header_include (lib/nginx/common.sh)

  • Entry points: path header handling.
  • Behavior: ensures header include file exists for a header set.

_real_ip_directives (lib/nginx/common.sh)

  • Entry points: config generation.
  • Behavior: emits real_ip_* directives based on trusted proxy ranges.

_client_ip_value_var (lib/nginx/common.sh)

  • Entry points: config generation.
  • Behavior: returns $proxy_add_x_forwarded_for for X-Forwarded-For (case-insensitive); otherwise returns $remote_addr so non-XFF client IP headers carry a trusted single client address.

_backend_header_identity_directives (lib/nginx/common.sh)

  • Entry points: config generation.
  • Behavior: emits per-server directives that bind backend header maps to the matched backend context, including alias- and dedicated-host-specific identities.

Module: certs (lib/certs/*.sh)

add_cert (lib/certs/add_cert.sh)

  • Entry points: CLI add-cert; internal HTTPS flows.
  • Inputs: domain, port_suffix, certificate type, optional paths.
  • Behavior: creates self-signed, Let's Encrypt, or uploaded certificates; ensures permissions; optionally auto-adds an HTTPS port mapping and HTTP redirect; skips the final nginx update when SKIP_UPDATE_NGINX_CONFIG=true (caller-controlled).
  • Certificate identity: newly generated self-signed certificates include a DNS SAN, or an IP SAN for an IPv4 host, using OpenSSL/LibreSSL-compatible configuration syntax.
  • Failure handling: a Certbot image-pull failure explicitly rolls back the transaction and releases its lock and traps, including when interactive dispatch checks the command's return status.
  • Validation mode: Certbot uses webroot only when the running managed proxy publishes HTTP port 80; otherwise it uses standalone validation.
  • Side effects: writes certificate files under CERTS_DIR, modifies BACKEND_PORTS_FILE, backups, update_nginx_config (unless skipped).
  • Interactive notes: picker prompts list backend/certificate domains, certificate suffixes, and certificate type before review; upload file paths are requested only when upload is selected.

replace_cert (lib/certs/replace_cert.sh)

  • Entry points: CLI replace-cert.
  • Behavior: refreshes certificate material and activates the proxy certificate projection without changing listeners or redirect choices. Domain storage retains the selected owner/ID; legacy storage removes superseded provider directories using safe-delete guards.
  • Side effects: updates managed certificate material, creates configured backups, and refreshes Nginx. Failed activation restores the previous material.
  • Interactive notes: uses the same domain, suffix, certificate type, and upload-path picker flow as add-cert.

list_certs (lib/certs/list_certs.sh)

  • Entry points: CLI list-certs, status-all.
  • Behavior: lists certificate directories, types, ports, and usage based on nginx config and port mappings.

remove_cert (lib/certs/remove_cert.sh)

  • Entry points: CLI and interactive remove-cert.
  • Behavior: removes certificate directories only if no port mappings depend on them; certificate/archive/renewal file deletions are validated by safe-delete guards; updates nginx when removal succeeds.
  • Backup finalization: requests the automatic snapshot after removal so its finalized editable/applied declarations exclude the certificate. Snapshot failure restores certificate material, declarations, and previous backup pointers.
  • Migration cleanup: removes matching retained legacy serving copies only after a successful explicit removal commits.
  • Side effects: deletes certificate directories, backups, update_nginx_config.
  • Interactive notes: lists known certificate domains and suffixes before destructive review; manual entry remains available for uncommon certificate suffixes.

renew_certs (lib/certs/renew_certs.sh)

  • Entry points: CLI renew-certs.
  • Behavior: scans HTTPS port mappings, checks expiration, renews Let's Encrypt certificates in window, refreshes nginx config.

_renew_letsencrypt_cert (lib/certs/_renew_letsencrypt_cert.sh)

  • Entry points: renew_certs.
  • Behavior: runs certbot in webroot or standalone mode; pulls certbot image per policy; refreshes nginx config before webroot renewal.
  • Side effects: runs Docker certbot, writes certificates under CERTS_DIR, may update_nginx_config.

_cert_expiring_soon (lib/certs/_cert_expiring_soon.sh)

  • Entry points: renew_certs.
  • Behavior: checks if a certificate expires within a window.

_notify_cert_warning (lib/certs/_notify_cert_warning.sh)

  • Entry points: renew_certs.
  • Behavior: logs warnings and optionally emails via mail or sendmail.

check_certbot_installed (lib/certs/check_certbot_installed.sh)

  • Entry points: certificate creation/renewal.
  • Behavior: no-op when using Docker-based certbot.

cert_created_timestamp (lib/certs/cert_created_timestamp.sh)

  • Entry points: list_certs.
  • Behavior: returns file mtime in a cross-platform way.

Module: TLS (lib/tls/*.sh)

set_tls_protocols (lib/tls/set_tls_protocols.sh)

  • Entry points: CLI set-tls-protocols.
  • Behavior: validates protocol list, stores global setting, updates nginx.

set_tls_ciphers (lib/tls/set_tls_ciphers.sh)

  • Entry points: CLI set-tls-ciphers.
  • Behavior: validates cipher-list data without letting leading-minus values become OpenSSL command options, rejects control characters and Nginx directive-breaking values, stores the global setting, and updates nginx. Valid operator-selected leading-minus rules remain supported while option-only values such as -v fail parsing.

set_port_tls_protocols (lib/tls/set_port_tls_protocols.sh)

  • Entry points: CLI set-port-tls-protocols.
  • Behavior: validates the HTTPS port mapping, stores per-port override, updates nginx.

remove_port_tls_protocols (lib/tls/remove_port_tls_protocols.sh)

remove_port_tls_ciphers (lib/tls/remove_port_tls_ciphers.sh)

get_port_tls_protocols (lib/tls/common.sh)

get_port_tls_ciphers (lib/tls/common.sh)

Module: headers (lib/headers/*.sh)

  • Mode scope: both CLI and interactive. Header identity is case-insensitive within each owner and request/response type; ordinary stored spelling, command/completion syntax, CSV formats, and escaping remain unchanged.
  • Identical-value case variants coalesce in generated views without rewriting source files. Conflicting values require an explicit setter/removal or a corrected draft and apply; different owners may retain different values.
  • Explicit repairs are staged before normal cache validation, then the complete candidate is validated before transactional publication. Target pending drafts, unrelated drafts, and concurrent edits remain protected, including edits to the shared state/config/custom_headers.csv during global or backend header commands; activation failures roll back while preserving newer editable content.

domain_config_header_command (lib/domain_config/header_mutations.sh)

  • Entry points: CLI and interactive header setters/removers, including HSTS/CSP and bulk removal, when domain-owned configuration is active.
  • Behavior: copies applied inputs privately, repairs the selected owner/type/name, and validates the complete candidate before publication. It checks source revisions before publication and journals both domain drafts and the shared global header file. Commit checks current files and edits through held original file descriptors; rollback restores prior runtime state while preserving newer editable content. If the original and replacement global files both changed, both are retained with actionable paths for recovery.
  • Side effects: transactionally publishes changed header sources/applied snapshots, derived caches and Nginx configuration; records backups and audit history. Other editable and applied header spellings remain unchanged.

set_header (lib/headers/set_header.sh)

  • Entry points: CLI add-header and update-header.
  • Behavior: validates header name, type, and value (rejects control characters), then stores one global header entry per type and case-insensitive name. Explicit add/update consolidates matching variants with the supplied value, including existing conflicts.
  • Side effects: updates CUSTOM_HEADERS_FILE, backups, update_nginx_config.

remove_header (lib/headers/remove_header.sh)

  • Entry points: CLI remove-header.
  • Behavior: removes every case variant of the selected global header within its request/response type.
  • Side effects: updates CUSTOM_HEADERS_FILE, backups, update_nginx_config.

list_headers (lib/headers/list_headers.sh)

  • Entry points: CLI list-headers.
  • Behavior: prints validated global headers with one row per type and case-insensitive name; identical variants coalesce without rewriting input and conflicting values fail with repair guidance.

set_backend_header (lib/headers/set_backend_header.sh)

  • Entry points: CLI add-backend-header and update-backend-header.
  • Behavior: validates backend, header, and value (rejects control characters), then stores one override per owner, type, and case-insensitive name. Explicit add/update consolidates matching variants with the supplied value; target pending drafts are never overwritten.
  • Side effects: updates BACKEND_HEADERS_FILE, backups, update_nginx_config.

remove_backend_header (lib/headers/remove_backend_header.sh)

  • Entry points: CLI remove-backend-header.
  • Behavior: removes every case variant of the selected header within its owner and request/response type, preserving pending drafts.
  • Side effects: updates BACKEND_HEADERS_FILE, backups, update_nginx_config.

list_backend_headers (lib/headers/list_backend_headers.sh)

  • Entry points: CLI list-backend-headers.
  • Behavior: lists validated backend headers (all or for a domain), coalescing identical variants within each owner/type and rejecting conflicting values with repair guidance.

remove_all_headers (lib/headers/remove_all_headers.sh)

  • Entry points: CLI remove-all-headers.
  • Behavior: clears global header list.
  • Side effects: updates CUSTOM_HEADERS_FILE, backups, update_nginx_config.

remove_all_backend_headers (lib/headers/remove_all_backend_headers.sh)

  • Entry points: CLI remove-all-backend-headers.
  • Behavior: clears backend header overrides (all or for a domain).
  • Side effects: updates BACKEND_HEADERS_FILE, backups, update_nginx_config.

get_global_header_value (lib/headers/common.sh)

  • Entry points: interactive defaults.
  • Behavior: validates and returns a global header value by type and case-insensitive name; identical variants coalesce and conflicting values fail with repair guidance.

get_backend_header_value (lib/headers/common.sh)

  • Entry points: interactive defaults.
  • Behavior: validates and returns an explicit backend header value by owner, type, and case-insensitive name; different owners remain independent and conflicting variants fail with repair guidance.

_header_name_identity (lib/headers/common.sh)

  • Entry points: header lookup, mutation, validation, interactive choices, and rendering.
  • Behavior: returns the ASCII-lowercase identity of a header name without changing its stored spelling or value.

_header_rows_add / _header_rows_find / _header_records (lib/headers/common.sh)

  • Entry points: header validation, lookup, and generated views.
  • Behavior: validates rows and coalesces identical raw values by owner/type/case-insensitive name, preserving first spelling and explicitly empty values. Conflicts identify the owner, type, name, and repair commands. Read-only canonical views accept reordered CSV columns without rewriting input.
  • Storage: caller-local indexed arrays isolate each operation and support Bash 3; repeated rendering cannot reuse stale entries.

set_hsts (lib/headers/set_hsts.sh)

  • Entry points: CLI set-hsts.
  • Behavior: sets or removes global HSTS header.

set_backend_hsts (lib/headers/set_backend_hsts.sh)

  • Entry points: CLI set-backend-hsts.
  • Behavior: sets or removes backend-specific HSTS header.

set_csp (lib/headers/set_csp.sh)

  • Entry points: CLI set-csp.
  • Behavior: sets or removes global CSP header.

set_backend_csp (lib/headers/set_backend_csp.sh)

  • Entry points: CLI set-backend-csp.
  • Behavior: sets or removes backend-specific CSP header.

set_client_ip_header (lib/headers/set_client_ip_header.sh)

  • Entry points: CLI set-client-ip-header.
  • Behavior: sets global client IP header (or disables), saves config, and replaces the managed proxy with config readiness checks; X-Forwarded-For uses chain semantics and other header names forward the trusted client address via $remote_addr. CLI and interactive changes interrupt active sessions so old identity trust is revoked.

set_proxy_ip_header (lib/headers/set_proxy_ip_header.sh)

  • Entry points: CLI set-proxy-ip-header.
  • Behavior: sets global proxy IP header (or disables), saves config, updates nginx.

set_backend_client_ip_header (lib/headers/set_backend_client_ip_header.sh)

  • Entry points: CLI set-backend-client-ip-header.
  • Behavior: sets per-backend client IP header override or disables; CLI and interactive changes replace the managed proxy with config readiness checks and interrupt active sessions.
  • Side effects: updates BACKEND_CLIENT_IP_HEADER_FILE, backups, _global_settings_update_nginx_config_for_security_change.

remove_backend_client_ip_header (lib/headers/remove_backend_client_ip_header.sh)

  • Entry points: CLI remove-backend-client-ip-header.
  • Behavior: removes per-backend client IP header override; CLI and interactive changes replace the managed proxy with config readiness checks and interrupt active sessions.
  • Side effects: updates BACKEND_CLIENT_IP_HEADER_FILE, backups, _global_settings_update_nginx_config_for_security_change.

set_backend_proxy_ip_header (lib/headers/set_backend_proxy_ip_header.sh)

  • Entry points: CLI set-backend-proxy-ip-header.
  • Behavior: sets per-backend proxy IP header override or disables.
  • Side effects: updates BACKEND_PROXY_IP_HEADER_FILE, backups, update_nginx_config.

remove_backend_proxy_ip_header (lib/headers/remove_backend_proxy_ip_header.sh)

  • Entry points: CLI remove-backend-proxy-ip-header.
  • Behavior: removes per-backend proxy IP header override.
  • Side effects: updates BACKEND_PROXY_IP_HEADER_FILE, backups, update_nginx_config.

get_backend_client_ip_header (lib/headers/common.sh)

  • Entry points: nginx config generation.
  • Behavior: returns per-backend client IP header override or global default.

get_backend_proxy_ip_header (lib/headers/common.sh)

  • Entry points: nginx config generation.
  • Behavior: returns per-backend proxy IP header override or global default.

_build_header_files (lib/headers/_build_header_files.sh)

  • Entry points: update_nginx_config.
  • Behavior: validates all persisted header rows before changing generated includes. Identical-value case variants coalesce into one global directive or backend map/directive per type and logical name; conflicting values fail with actionable repair guidance. Backend maps retain each owner's value and use the server-local backend identity variable. Dedicated-host overrides suppress inherited variants regardless of capitalization.
  • Backend request/response maps preserve escaped double quotes and backslashes without interpreting escape sequences again, including inherited dedicated-host values. Nginx variable interpretation is unchanged; CLI and interactive updates use the same renderer.
  • Upgrade: existing saved header values are retained. Run update-nginx-config to regenerate maps from applied settings and activate corrected escaping, then check-config.

_escape_header_value (lib/headers/common.sh)

  • Entry points: header file generation.
  • Behavior: escapes backslashes and quotes for Nginx config values.

_validate_persisted_header_row (lib/headers/common.sh)

  • Entry points: _build_header_files.
  • Behavior: fail-closed validation for persisted global/backend header rows before config rendering.

Module: security_rules (lib/security_rules/*.sh)

add_security_rule (lib/security_rules/add_security_rule.sh)

  • Entry points: CLI and interactive add-security-rule.
  • Inputs: domain, count or mode, condition tuples (source, name, condition, value), optional --action block|require|allow, --mode, --code, --reason, and --loc. CLI calls without --action retain the Require default; interactive creation explicitly selects an action.
  • Targets: applied backends, ordinary aliases, and dedicated hosts. Host-specific rules stay local to the named host; the target is rechecked under the mutation lock.
  • Behavior: validates domain, selector names, and operators, rejects CIDR values for ip|ip:l7|ip:l3 selectors (equals, not_equals, in, not_in), enforces numeric comparisons only for var: selectors, writes an escaped rule line with the chosen action. Options are parsed outside complete condition tuples so literal condition values such as --action remain data.
  • Side effects: appends to SECURITY_RULES_DB, backups, update_nginx_config.

update_security_rule (lib/security_rules/update_security_rule.sh)

  • Entry points: CLI and interactive update-security-rule.
  • Behavior: loads rule by ID, updates action/domain/mode/code/count and condition tuples, preserves the existing action when --action is absent, validates selector names and operators, rejects CIDR values for ip|ip:l7|ip:l3 selectors, rewrites line.
  • Targets: --domain accepts applied backends, aliases, and dedicated hosts. Pending edits are checked for both the original and destination domain, and destination existence is rechecked under the mutation lock.
  • Side effects: updates SECURITY_RULES_DB, backups, update_nginx_config.

set_security_rule_mode (lib/security_rules/set_security_rule_mode.sh)

  • Entry points: CLI set-security-rule-mode.
  • Behavior: changes mode for multi-condition rules only.
  • Side effects: updates SECURITY_RULES_DB, backups, update_nginx_config.

list_security_rules (lib/security_rules/list_security_rules.sh)

  • Entry points: CLI list-security-rules, status, status-all.
  • Interactive parity: the listing picker offers All domains, configured backends/aliases/dedicated hosts, and manual domain entry. All domains passes no argument. A domain filter lists directly owned rows rather than expanding inherited policy, and keeps the global numeric IDs.
  • Behavior: prints rules with globally ordered numeric IDs, explicit action and conditions; domain filtering never renumbers IDs. The listing explains that Require rules run first, then the first matching Block/Allow decision wins. Allow has no rejection code.

remove_security_rule (lib/security_rules/remove_security_rule.sh)

  • Entry points: CLI remove-security-rule.
  • Behavior: deletes a rule by line number.
  • Side effects: updates SECURITY_RULES_DB, backups, update_nginx_config.

remove_all_security_rules (lib/security_rules/remove_all_security_rules.sh)

  • Entry points: CLI remove-all-security-rules.
  • Behavior: clears rule DB.
  • Side effects: updates SECURITY_RULES_DB, backups, update_nginx_config.

enable_security_rule (lib/security_rules/enable_security_rule.sh)

  • Entry points: CLI enable-security-rule.
  • Behavior: sets enabled flag to 1 for the target rule line.
  • Side effects: create_backup and update_nginx_config.

disable_security_rule (lib/security_rules/disable_security_rule.sh)

  • Entry points: CLI disable-security-rule.
  • Behavior: sets enabled flag to 0 for the target rule line.
  • Side effects: create_backup and update_nginx_config.

enable_all_security_rules (lib/security_rules/enable_all_security_rules.sh)

  • Entry points: CLI enable-all-security-rules.
  • Behavior: sets enabled flag to 1 for all rule lines.
  • Side effects: create_backup and update_nginx_config.

disable_all_security_rules (lib/security_rules/disable_all_security_rules.sh)

  • Entry points: CLI disable-all-security-rules.
  • Behavior: sets enabled flag to 0 for all rule lines.
  • Side effects: create_backup and update_nginx_config.

duplicate_security_rule (lib/security_rules/duplicate_security_rule.sh)

  • Entry points: CLI duplicate-security-rule.
  • Behavior: appends a copy of an existing rule and reports new ID.
  • Side effects: appends to SECURITY_RULES_DB, backups, update_nginx_config.

move_security_rule (lib/security_rules/move_security_rule.sh)

  • Entry points: CLI move-security-rule.
  • Behavior: reorders rules by line number.
  • Side effects: reorders SECURITY_RULES_DB, backups, update_nginx_config.

build_security_rules_inc (lib/security_rules/build_security_rules_inc.sh)

  • Entry points: update_nginx_config.
  • Behavior: regenerates security_rules.inc and per-domain ACL includes. All applicable Require rules run first in their saved relative order. Block/Allow rules then run in global numeric order; the first match rejects (Block) or skips only later Block/Allow rules (Allow). No match continues normal processing. Allow never bypasses Require, ACL, or mTLS checks. Each backend rule expands to aliases and dedicated hosts with security-rule inheritance enabled, preserving order and recipient-specific variables. Rejection codes use the explicit rule code or each recipient's effective status. Invalid actions, predicates, topology, inheritance, or enabled unknown identities stop generation. The decision latch resets on each include evaluation, including internal redirects; existing proxied-HTTP-location scope is unchanged.

_build_security_rules_phase (lib/security_rules/build_security_rules_inc.sh)

  • Entry points: build_security_rules_inc.
  • Behavior: validates and renders the selected Require or Block/Allow phase, retaining original global IDs and ordering before expanding inheritance recipients. Disabled rules remain validated but emit no decision.

_generate_security_decision_line (lib/security_rules/_sr_builders.sh)

  • Entry points: _build_security_rules_phase for Block/Allow rules.
  • Behavior: combines positive predicates using single/AND/OR matching, then checks the serving identity and prior decision latch. A matching Block returns its configured rejection; a matching Allow sets the latch without ending rewrite/access processing. It uses escaped values and flat Nginx conditions, preserving ACL/mTLS and later location handling.

_sr_rule_recipients (lib/security_rules/_sr_identity.sh)

  • Entry points: standalone identity resolution; build_security_rules_inc uses _sr_rule_recipients_validated after validating the complete alias table once.
  • Behavior: returns a rule's own identity and, for a backend rule, its ordinary aliases and inheriting dedicated hosts. Host-specific persisted rules are additive and do not propagate back to the primary.

_sr_rule_recipients_validated (lib/security_rules/_sr_identity.sh)

  • Entry points: build_security_rules_inc, _sr_rule_recipients.
  • Behavior: enumerates recipients after alias-table validation, rejecting unknown identities and malformed dedicated-host inheritance.

_sr_identity_directives (lib/security_rules/_sr_identity.sh)

  • Entry points: backend and dedicated-host HTTP/HTTPS server rendering.
  • Behavior: validates topology and binds dockistrate_security_identity to the selected server. Only registered aliases in that serving block may select an alternate identity; request Host and SNI variables remain unchanged.

build_security_ip_includes (lib/security_rules/build_security_ip_includes.sh)

  • Entry points: build_security_rules_inc.
  • Behavior: writes per-domain HTTP and stream include files from IP rules. ACL variable names are bounded and deterministic, with collision handling in sorted host order independent of request-rule variables. Ordinary aliases with enabled rules or policy/status overrides get HTTP includes consumed by their separate serving blocks; inactive alias includes and unused alias stream includes are removed.

_acl_inherited_domain (lib/security_rules/_acl_identity.sh)

  • Entry points: ACL getters, rule generation, and CIDR transition validation.
  • Behavior: resolves the primary backend for an ordinary alias, or an ACL-inheriting dedicated host; returns an empty result for identities using global defaults and propagates invalid inheritance state.

_alias_has_explicit_acl (lib/security_rules/_acl_identity.sh)

  • Entry points: ACL include generation and HTTP/HTTPS serving-block selection.
  • Behavior: distinguishes enabled alias ACL rules or explicit policy/status overrides from primary fallback; invalid active alias rules fail generation instead of silently selecting the primary policy.

_build_security_ip_for_domain (lib/security_rules/_sr_builders.sh)

  • Entry points: build_security_ip_includes.
  • Behavior: emits allow/deny directives and conditional returns for L7/L3 ACL policies and status codes (including both scope). Aliases and inheriting dedicated hosts use the primary rule list only when no enabled own rules remain; explicit policy/status overrides are independent.
  • Precedence: matching explicit denies override overlapping allows. The HTTP 403 access-directive branch emits denies first, then allows, then the policy fallback; custom-status and L3 conditional returns retain their existing behavior. Explicit deny 0.0.0.0/0 is a rule rather than the generated default-deny fallback. See ACL precedence and upgrade steps.

_build_security_ip_stream_for_domain (lib/security_rules/_sr_builders.sh)

  • Entry points: build_security_ip_includes.
  • Behavior: emits stream allow/deny directives for ACL rules (L7/L3 scopes map to client IP; status codes ignored).
  • Precedence: explicit denies precede all allows, including narrower matching allows, and the default-deny fallback remains last. The same ordering applies to TCP and UDP listeners.

add_security_ip (lib/security_rules/add_security_ip.sh)

  • Entry points: CLI add-acl (aliased).
  • Inputs: domain, scope (l7|l3|both), action (allow|deny), IPs, optional status code.
  • Behavior: validates domain/IPv4, pre-validates all tokens before writing, rejects CIDR values for l3 and both scopes, rejects non-403 status overrides for L7 CIDR deny rules, rejects exact duplicates both within the current request and against persisted ACL rows (same domain/scope/action/ip/code), then appends rule(s) to SECURITY_IP_RULES_DB.
  • Side effects: updates SECURITY_IP_RULES_DB, backups, update_nginx_config.

update_security_ip (lib/security_rules/update_security_ip.sh)

  • Entry points: CLI update-acl (aliased), interactive Update ACL through the same flag-based update implementation.
  • Behavior: updates a security IP rule by ID, validates scope/action/IPv4/code (l7|l3|both), rejects CIDR values for l3 and both, and rejects final L7 CIDR deny rules with non-403 status overrides.
  • Side effects: updates SECURITY_IP_RULES_DB, backups, update_nginx_config.

list_security_ip (lib/security_rules/list_security_ip.sh)

  • Entry points: CLI list-acl (aliased), status, status-all.
  • Behavior: lists IP rules and indicates disabled status.

remove_security_ip (lib/security_rules/remove_security_ip.sh)

  • Entry points: CLI remove-acl (aliased).
  • Behavior: removes IP rule by ID.
  • Side effects: updates SECURITY_IP_RULES_DB, backups, update_nginx_config.

enable_security_ip_rule (lib/security_rules/enable_security_ip_rule.sh)

  • Entry points: CLI enable-acl (aliased).
  • Behavior: removes the leading comment marker from the rule line.
  • Side effects: create_backup and update_nginx_config.

disable_security_ip_rule (lib/security_rules/disable_security_ip_rule.sh)

  • Entry points: CLI disable-acl (aliased).
  • Behavior: prefixes the rule line with # to disable it.
  • Side effects: create_backup and update_nginx_config.

enable_all_security_ip_rules (lib/security_rules/enable_all_security_ip_rules.sh)

  • Entry points: CLI enable-all-acl (aliased).
  • Behavior: removes leading comment markers from all rule lines.
  • Side effects: create_backup and update_nginx_config.

disable_all_security_ip_rules (lib/security_rules/disable_all_security_ip_rules.sh)

  • Entry points: CLI disable-all-acl (aliased).
  • Behavior: prefixes all non-empty, non-comment lines with #.
  • Side effects: create_backup and update_nginx_config.

remove_all_security_ip_rules (lib/security_rules/remove_all_security_ip_rules.sh)

  • Entry points: CLI remove-all-acl (aliased).
  • Behavior: clears the IP rules file.
  • Side effects: updates SECURITY_IP_RULES_DB, backups, update_nginx_config.

move_security_ip_rule (lib/security_rules/move_security_ip_rule.sh)

  • Entry points: CLI move-acl-rule (aliased).
  • Behavior: reorders IP rules by line number.
  • Precedence: moving an allow before a matching deny does not bypass deny-overrides precedence.
  • Side effects: reorders SECURITY_IP_RULES_DB, backups, update_nginx_config.

set_acl_policy (lib/security_rules/set_acl_policy.sh)

  • Entry points: CLI set-acl-policy.
  • Behavior: sets global allow/deny policy and updates nginx; blocks deny when effective ACL status is non-403 and CIDR allow ACL rules are present.
  • Upgrade use: reapplying the current policy value regenerates ACLs and replaces the managed proxy, including existing sessions; per-host overrides remain unchanged. Review overlapping deny/allow rows before applying the precedence change.

get_backend_acl_policy (lib/security_rules/get_backend_acl_policy.sh)

  • Entry points: config generation and prompts.
  • Behavior: returns an explicit ACL policy override, otherwise the primary backend's override for an alias or inheriting dedicated host, otherwise global policy.

set_backend_acl_policy (lib/security_rules/set_backend_acl_policy.sh)

  • Entry points: CLI set-backend-acl-policy.
  • Behavior: stores an ACL policy override for a backend, alias, or dedicated host; blocks deny when effective ACL status is non-403 and CIDR allow ACL rules are present, including aliases and inheriting dedicated hosts mapped to that backend.
  • Side effects: updates BACKEND_ACL_POLICY_FILE, backups, update_nginx_config.

remove_backend_acl_policy (lib/security_rules/remove_backend_acl_policy.sh)

  • Entry points: CLI remove-backend-acl-policy.
  • Behavior: removes per-backend ACL policy override.
  • Side effects: updates BACKEND_ACL_POLICY_FILE, backups, update_nginx_config.

get_backend_acl_status (lib/security_rules/get_backend_acl_status.sh)

  • Entry points: config generation and prompts.
  • Behavior: returns an explicit ACL status override, otherwise the primary backend's override for an alias or inheriting dedicated host, otherwise global status.

set_backend_acl_status (lib/security_rules/set_backend_acl_status.sh)

  • Entry points: CLI set-backend-acl-status.
  • Behavior: stores an ACL status override for a backend, alias, or dedicated host; blocks non-403 codes when effective ACL policy is deny and CIDR allow ACL rules are present, including aliases and inheriting dedicated hosts mapped to that backend.
  • Side effects: updates BACKEND_ACL_STATUS_FILE, backups, update_nginx_config.

remove_backend_acl_status (lib/security_rules/remove_backend_acl_status.sh)

  • Entry points: CLI remove-backend-acl-status.
  • Behavior: removes per-backend ACL status override.
  • Side effects: updates BACKEND_ACL_STATUS_FILE, backups, update_nginx_config.

get_backend_security_rule_status (lib/security_rules/get_backend_security_rule_status.sh)

  • Entry points: config generation and prompts.
  • Behavior: returns an explicit serving-host status, otherwise the primary override for an ordinary alias or security-rule-inheriting dedicated host, otherwise the global status. Invalid saved status or inheritance propagates an error.

set_backend_security_rule_status (lib/security_rules/set_backend_security_rule_status.sh)

  • Entry points: CLI set-backend-security-rule-status.
  • Behavior: stores a security-rule status override for a backend, alias, or dedicated host; both interactive choices and completion expose these identities. Explicit per-rule codes retain precedence.
  • Side effects: updates BACKEND_SECURITY_RULE_STATUS_FILE, backups, update_nginx_config.

remove_backend_security_rule_status (lib/security_rules/remove_backend_security_rule_status.sh)

  • Entry points: CLI remove-backend-security-rule-status.
  • Behavior: removes per-backend security rule status override.
  • Side effects: updates BACKEND_SECURITY_RULE_STATUS_FILE, backups, update_nginx_config.

condition_alias (lib/security_rules/_sr_strings.sh)

  • Entry points: interactive prompts.
  • Behavior: returns title-cased label for condition names.

_sr_escape (lib/security_rules/_sr_strings.sh)

  • Entry points: DB write helpers.
  • Behavior: escapes user input for safe Nginx expression construction and regex generation.

_sr_unescape (lib/security_rules/_sr_strings.sh)

  • Entry points: DB read helpers.
  • Behavior: decodes escaped selector/value fragments used during rule-expression generation.

_sr_write_db_line (lib/security_rules/_sr_db.sh)

  • Entry points: historical callers and configuration migration.
  • Behavior: writes a schema-aligned Require rule through _sr_write_db_line_with_action. Historical 47-column encoding is available only in explicitly scoped migration/recovery codecs.

_sr_write_db_line_with_action (lib/security_rules/_sr_db.sh)

  • Entry points: rule creation/update and per-domain compilation.
  • Behavior: accepts an explicit action, followed by the existing rule fields, and appends the normalized action as column 48 without changing earlier field positions. Rejects Block/Allow in historical codecs.

_sr_normalize_action (lib/security_rules/_sr_db.sh)

  • Entry points: rule parsing, generation and persistence.
  • Behavior: accepts block, require, or allow; blank means require. Rejects unknown values.

_sr_load_line (lib/security_rules/_sr_db.sh)

  • Entry points: rule update/enable/disable.
  • Behavior: loads a rule line by line number.

_sr_delete_line (lib/security_rules/_sr_db.sh)

  • Entry points: rule removal.
  • Behavior: deletes a line from DB.

_sr_replace_line (lib/security_rules/_sr_db.sh)

  • Entry points: rule update and toggles.
  • Behavior: replaces a line by line number.

_sr_source_to_selector (lib/security_rules/_sr_selectors.sh)

  • Entry points: rule validation and generation.
  • Behavior: maps source + optional name to a selector string.

_sr_selector_to_var (lib/security_rules/_sr_selectors.sh)

  • Entry points: rule generation.
  • Behavior: maps selector to Nginx variable and label.

_sr_allowed_ops_for_selector (lib/security_rules/_sr_selectors.sh)

  • Entry points: validation and interactive filtering.
  • Behavior: returns allowed conditions per selector type.

_sr_validate_selector_condition (lib/security_rules/_sr_selectors.sh)

  • Entry points: rule validation.
  • Behavior: errors when condition not allowed for selector.

_sr_validate_selector_name (lib/security_rules/common.sh)

  • Entry points: rule validation.
  • Behavior: validates header, cookie, arg, and var selector names before save or persisted render.

_sr_validate_acl_cidr_deny_status (lib/security_rules/common.sh)

  • Entry points: add_security_ip, update_security_ip.
  • Behavior: rejects L7 CIDR deny ACL rules with non-403 status overrides because Nginx CIDR deny rules always return 403.

_sr_exprs (lib/security_rules/_sr_selectors.sh)

  • Entry points: rule generation.
  • Behavior: returns Nginx predicate fragments for a condition and value.

_sr_next_rule_var (lib/security_rules/_sr_db.sh)

  • Entry points: rule generation.
  • Behavior: increments a counter and provides a unique variable prefix.

_sr_numeric_inc (lib/security_rules/_sr_numeric.sh)

  • Entry points: numeric comparisons.
  • Behavior: increments a numeric string.

_sr_numeric_regex_ge (lib/security_rules/_sr_numeric.sh)

  • Entry points: numeric comparisons.
  • Behavior: builds regex that matches numbers >= input.

_sr_numeric_regex_ge_same (lib/security_rules/_sr_numeric.sh)

  • Entry points: numeric comparisons.
  • Behavior: helper to build regex for same-length numbers >= input.

_sr_trim_leading_zeros (lib/security_rules/_sr_numeric.sh)

  • Entry points: numeric comparisons.
  • Behavior: strips leading zeros.

_sr_is_unsigned_int (lib/security_rules/_sr_numeric.sh)

  • Entry points: numeric comparisons.
  • Behavior: validates unsigned integer.

_sr_escape_regex_literal (lib/security_rules/_sr_strings.sh)

  • Entry points: regex condition building.
  • Behavior: escapes regex metacharacters.

_sr_assert_domain_exists (lib/security_rules/_sr_db.sh)

  • Entry points: rule creation/update.
  • Behavior: validates that the named backend, ordinary alias, or dedicated host exists in applied state.

_escape_nginx_value (lib/security_rules/_sr_strings.sh)

  • Entry points: rule generation.
  • Behavior: escapes quotes and backslashes for Nginx configs.

_generate_security_rule_line (lib/security_rules/_sr_builders.sh)

  • Entry points: build_security_rules_inc.
  • Behavior: emits a single-condition Nginx rule gated by the configured dockistrate_security_identity, preserving request variables used by predicates.

_generate_security_rule_multi_line (lib/security_rules/_sr_builders.sh)

  • Entry points: build_security_rules_inc.
  • Behavior: gates multi-condition logic by the configured dockistrate_security_identity; denies or rules only when all predicates fail and denies and rules whenever any predicate fails.

_is_ip (lib/security_rules/_sr_builders.sh)

  • Entry points: ACL policy generation.
  • Behavior: detects IPv4 dotted-quad patterns.

Module: mtls (lib/mtls/*.sh)

enable_backend_mtls (lib/mtls/enable_backend_mtls.sh)

  • Entry points: CLI and interactive enable-backend-mtls.
  • Behavior: validates the domain and owned mTLS path, distinguishes a new authority from retained or previously enabled state, and validates existing authority/database material before reuse. Only first-time setup with no retained authority material creates a CA and initializes its database. Missing identity/history files never trigger replacement keys or reset counters. Stores the domain mapping, optionally issues a client certificate, generates the CRL from validated state, and updates nginx transactionally.
  • Side effects: creates or updates owned files under state/domains/<domain>/mtls (legacy layout: CERTS_DIR/mtls/<domain>) and updates BACKEND_MTLS_FILE.

disable_backend_mtls (lib/mtls/disable_backend_mtls.sh)

  • Entry points: CLI disable-backend-mtls.
  • Behavior: validates and normalizes the domain, removes the matching domain mapping from BACKEND_MTLS_FILE, and updates nginx.

add_backend_client_cert (lib/mtls/add_backend_client_cert.sh)

  • Entry points: CLI and interactive add-backend-client-cert.
  • Behavior: validates the domain and client name, resolves the exact owner-bound mTLS directory (including valid dedicated-host inheritance), requires intact authority/database material, issues a client certificate signed by the owner CA, and updates the CRL.
  • Side effects: writes client certificate files/CRL, update_nginx_config.

remove_backend_client_cert (lib/mtls/remove_backend_client_cert.sh)

  • Entry points: CLI and interactive remove-backend-client-cert.
  • Behavior: validates the domain and client name, resolves the exact owner-bound mTLS directory, validates its existing authority/database, revokes a certificate, and deletes client files.
  • Side effects: updates CRL and client files, update_nginx_config.

revoke_backend_client_cert (lib/mtls/revoke_backend_client_cert.sh)

  • Entry points: CLI and interactive revoke-backend-client-cert.
  • Behavior: validates the domain and client name, resolves the exact owner-bound mTLS directory, validates its existing authority/database, and revokes a certificate while keeping its files.
  • Side effects: updates CRL, update_nginx_config.

replace_backend_client_cert (lib/mtls/replace_backend_client_cert.sh)

  • Entry points: CLI and interactive replace-backend-client-cert.
  • Behavior: validates the domain and client name, resolves the exact owner-bound mTLS directory, validates its existing authority/database, and removes and re-issues a client certificate.
  • Side effects: updates client certificate files/CRL, update_nginx_config.

export_backend_client_p12 (lib/mtls/export_backend_client_p12.sh)

  • Entry points: CLI and interactive export-backend-client-p12.
  • Behavior: validates the domain and client name, resolves the owner-bound mTLS directory, validates its existing authority/database without initializing or repairing files, validates --password-env names before indirect expansion, requires a non-empty single-line password from the selected source (password files may end with one LF or CRLF), and exports a PKCS#12 bundle.

list_backend_client_certs (lib/mtls/list_backend_client_certs.sh)

  • Entry points: CLI and interactive list-backend-client-certs.
